News.title: Prisoners freed early are returning to jail at rapid rate, governors tell BBC
News.content:
Prisoners who were freed under the government's last early release scheme are returning to jail at a rapid rate, prison governors have told the BBC.

They say they are seeing the same inmates, who were let out as part of the 2024 early release scheme to ease overcrowding, coming back after reoffending - including for breaching their conditions.

"The churn is what stresses me out," said one governor in the Midlands, describing it as a "revolving door".

It comes as Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced changes to the next early release scheme, starting in October, following outrage that the killers of PC Andrew Harper were among those eligible to be released.

On Sunday, Burnham announced that they will not be, telling the BBC that anyone convicted of unlawful killing will be excluded from the scheme.

He conceded that it means "hundreds" more people will stay in prison - as prisons in England and Wales reach breaking point at more than 97% full.

The government says there are plans to create more prison space by deporting foreign inmates and releasing some who are serving indefinite sentences, but they are unlikely to create much more space by the time the first batch of inmates are released in October.

BBC News spoke to three serving prison governors in England to gauge the state of correctional facilities and how staff are dealing with overcrowding. Prison staff are not supposed to speak to the media so their names and the prisons they govern will not be mentioned to protect their identity.

One governor from a prison in the north of England said the PM's plans to ease overcrowding "is all short-term solutions and we need space now".

"Providing additional cells in existing prisons will mean more prison staff needed to monitor that - it's not easy," they said, adding that staff shortages mean "prisoners are not living in a safe and decent environment".

The governor also said they were frustrated by the rate of prisoner recalls, saying: "We see the same people coming back after being released early and reoffending again, or breaking their [release] rules."

News.title: Patel to be replaced by Tugendhat as shadow foreign secretary
News.content:
Former Tory leadership candidate Tom Tugendhat will replace Dame Priti Patel as shadow foreign secretary, BBC News has been told.

As first reported by the Daily Telegraph, he will return to the Conservative front bench when Kemi Badenoch reshuffles her team next month.

Dame Priti wrote on social media that she would be leaving the role to take up a new position designed to "strengthen links with sister parties and centre right movements around the world".

It comes a day after shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said he was resigning in order to run for London mayor.

The move will see Tugendhat return to a senior role for the first time since finishing fourth in the 2024 Tory leadership election.

The former British Army reserve and Territorial Army officer has long been vocal on international affairs and security matters.

He served as security minister under Liz Truss and Boris Johnson and prior to that spent five years as chair of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee.

Dame Priti was appointed to Badenoch's shadow cabinet after finishing sixth in the leadership election.

She held senior roles in successive Tory governments, including a three-year spell as home secretary under Boris Johnson.

A Conservative reshuffle had already been expected in the coming weeks because of the shadow energy secretary Claire Coutinho's upcoming maternity leave.

In recent weeks, people within the party have played down speculation that the shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride could also lose his job in the changes.

But some sources within the party still believe Badenoch could choose to replace him.

Many within the Conservative Party view Coutinho as a likely future shadow chancellor. The shadow energy secretary is said to have impressed colleagues with her performances in Parliament and the media.

But it is unlikely Badenoch will move to appoint her as shadow chancellor while she is on leave from the front bench.

News.title: UK raises case of British activist detained by settlers in West Bank with Israel
News.content:
The UK Foreign Office says it has raised the detention of a British national in the occupied West Bank with Israeli authorities.

Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old student activist, was arrested in Umm Al-Kheir on Saturday after he was forcibly detained by Israeli settlers who had advanced on the Palestinian village.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are also illegal under Israeli law, although they are often supported by state services and funding.

The confrontation on Saturday took place in a town near Hebron that has been recently surrounded by settlers.

According to other activists who witnessed what happened, Palestinian children were playing football when children from settler families started intervening. They then ran to a house and started to dismantle a fence.

Footage posted online by both settlers and activists and seen by the BBC appears to show Joughin standing by the fence and trying to protect it using his body as a child pushes against him.

Settlers removed Joughin forcefully and took the London-based student to an outpost.

Israeli police said a foreign national was detained by security personnel of a settler community who suspected him of an indecent act against a minor.

In a later statement on Sunday, they said: "The suspect was transferred to the police for questioning, which included, among other things, taking statements that raised suspicion of an assault against a minor.

"Following his questioning, the suspect was taken into custody, and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing."

However, Joughin's family told the BBC he was due to be deported from Israel on Monday.

Activists who were with Joughin at the time deny there was any inappropriate behaviour.

"In every single instance, it was the settler kids who approached Finn," fellow activist Matthew, who declined to give his surname, told the BBC.

News.title: The mystery of why so many black Britons still can't swim
News.content:
As I push through the doors, the smell of chlorine hits me. Instantly, I feel sick, and I remember why I don't go swimming. I'm getting ready for my first swimming lesson in over 10 years, trying to convince myself it won't be so bad.

Before I know it, I'm in the water.

I glance around the pool; I'm surrounded by other black women learning to swim, all at different levels. Some are confidently swimming lengths; others, like me, are learning how to feel at home in the water.

I'm learning to breathe properly, dunk my head under and let the water carry me, rather than fight against it. There are so many things to remember.

At the age of 27, I'm still unable to swim - and I'm far from alone.

Swimming ability is not spread evenly across the population; figures compiled by Swim England, swimming's governing body, based on a survey of 4,500 people suggest poorer people, for example, are much less likely to be able to swim, as well as Muslims, people of South Asian descent and children known to social care.

As a black woman, it's the figures for the black community that always jump out to me. Swim England's figures suggest that 67% of black women and 44% of black men in England cannot swim 25 metres unaided - far higher than the national average, and far higher than the numbers for white people (17% of white women and 12% of white men cannot swim 25 metres). Behind those figures, published in 2022, are very different stories.

News.title: Sons of officer who died in A66 crash lead out Man Utd as mascots
News.content:
The two sons of a police officer killed in a crash on Teesside led out the Manchester United team as mascots for Sunday's Premier League match against Ipswich at Old Trafford.

PC Matthew Blades, described as a "proud Red" by United, was a regular at Old Trafford.

The club paid tribute to him in Sunday's match programme, while his widow attended the game with their children.

PC Blades and his colleague PC Tom Clough died in a head-on collision between their police car and a vehicle going the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough early on 22 August. Five people in the other vehicle also died.

United said they learned of the deaths of the two officers "with great sadness".

"Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others," said the club, in a tribute in the programme.

At Elland Road, match officials for Leeds United's Premier League fixture against Brentford on Sunday wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades.

On Saturday, there was a minute's applause in memory of PC Blades and PC Clough before Middlesbrough's Championship encounter with West Brom at Riverside Stadium. Pictures of the two men were displayed on a screen.

People also gathered to pay tribute at Seaton Carew FC's game against FC Hartlepool. PC Blades had been a junior football coach at both teams.

Earlier this week, 17 people were arrested in connection with the investigation into the crash, bringing the total number of arrests to 24.

The occupants of the other vehicle, a Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17, also died.

News.title: Jewish community in harder position than immediately after synagogue attack, says rabbi
News.content:
The Jewish community at a synagogue where two men were killed in 2025 feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack, its rabbi has said almost one year on.

Rabbi Daniel Walker said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation in Manchester â and British Jews more widely â feeling increasingly vulnerable as the anniversary of the attack approaches.

"I think we're actually almost in a harder position than we were even immediately after the attack," he said ahead of a memorial service for the victims and survivors which will take place later today.

"I think the sense of vulnerability has grown. It hasn't diminished."

Two men, Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, were killed and three others were injured as they tried to defend their synagogue from attacker Jihad al-Shamie on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, on 2 October 2025.

A wave of worldwide attacks followed over subsequent months.

In Sydney, Australia, 15 people were killed in a shooting at a celebration for the festival of Chanukah on Bondi Beach.

In London, Jewish people and property were targeted in arson attacks, including in March on ambulances belonging to the Hatzola emergency medical service.

In April, two orthodox Jewish men were stabbed as they left morning prayers in Golders Green.

A BBC Freedom of Information request to police forces in England and Wales has found that across 33 forces, violent hate crimes targeting Jewish people â such as harassment and assault â have risen by nearly two thirds since 2022.

News.title: British woman killed in stabbing at German railway station
News.content:
A British woman has died after being stabbed at a railway station in southern Germany in the early hours of Sunday morning, police have said.

The 31-year-old woman was attacked at the station in Rosenheim, Bavaria, shortly before 01:00 local time (00:00 BST). She was taken to hospital where she died as a result of "severe" injuries, the Bavarian Police said in a statement.

Officers arrested a 27-year-old German man at the scene immediately after the incident. The background and motive for the attack is under investigation, the statement added.

Police have asked anyone who may have witnessed "an argument or physical altercation" at the station late on Saturday or early on Sunday to contact them.

The suspect, from the FÃ¼rstenfeldbruck district, will be brought before magistrates later on Sunday, according to German news agency DPA.

It is unclear whether the two knew each other or what the woman was doing in Bavaria, DPA also reported.

Rosenheim is one of the largest cities in Upper Bavaria and is a busy rail hub for passengers travelling to Austrian cities including Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck.

The Rosenheimer Herbstfest - an event similar to the Oktoberfest beer festival - is currently taking place in the area.

Responding to the attack, Rosenheim Mayor Abuzar Erdogan said "there are no indications of a security threat in our city or of any link to our Herbstfest".

"The criminal investigation department is working closely with the public prosecutor's office to investigate the circumstances and motive behind the crime as a matter of urgency," he wrote in a statement.

A Foreign Office spokesperson told the BBC: "We are supporting the family of a British woman who died in Germany [and] are in touch with the local authorities."

News.title: Seven arrested after death of newborn baby girl
News.content:
Seven people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after the death of a newborn baby girl in Sheffield, police said.

Officers were called at about 06:00 BST on Sunday to a property on Holywell Heights in the Wincobank area following reports of a concern for the safety of the baby.

South Yorkshire Police said, despite the best efforts of officers and paramedics, the baby was pronounced dead at the scene.

Det Ch Insp Emma Knight confirmed the force was "working to determine the ages of some of those arrested".

She said: "We are aware news of this will be deeply concerning and I want to reassure our local communities that we have a dedicated team of detectives and officers hard at work to ensure justice is secured for the baby girl at the heart of this investigation."

Knight added: "Our investigation is in its early stages and we would like to remind people to avoid speculating about this incident."

News.title: Burnham gets the early prison release changes he wanted - but at what cost?
News.content:
The prime minister's announcement that he will keep hundreds of criminals behind bars who would otherwise have been released early is one he has wanted to make for weeks.

Andy Burnham had already expanded the list of people ineligible for early release and had consistently said he wanted to go further.

What is not clear is exactly what has changed to allow him to do so.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Justice warned that exempting any more prisoners risked "prisons reaching capacity and collapsing".

The prime minister himself previously said he had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".

In his exclusive interview with BBC Breakfast, Burnham picked out the release of people on controversial indefinite sentences and the deportation of foreign criminals as measures that had made his latest intervention possible.

It is understood extra capacity will also be created by immediately beginning work to create new cells in existing prisons.

But none of these are short-term solutions.

Ending indefinite sentences will require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

Previous governments have struggled to quickly deport foreign offenders and there are not thought to be any new returns agreements with other countries. The case of grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed, who Pakistan has resisted attempts to deport, is one example.

Retrofitting prisons to create more cells is also expected to take months.

People in government concede that in the short-term, Burnham will only be able to follow through on today's announcement by making prisons even more full.

With the adult male prison estate already running at 98% capacity, it is a move that could worry some in the sector.

But in the end, the prime minister believed he simply had to act.

The extra exemptions Burnham has announced are being described within government as a "political decision".

That is not surprising given the intense pressure that had built up, especially around the potential for PC Andrew Harper's killers to be released early.

Burnham's inner circle are mindful that political misjudgements at the start of Sir Keir Starmer's premiership caused long-lasting damage.

They believe Sir Keir never recovered from early rows over freebies and winter fuel payments, and point to a lack of major mishaps in Burnham's first six weeks in office as evidence of a more slick political operation.

There was some surprise in Downing Street about how much media attention the issue of early release received over the summer.

That is one reason why the prime minister's aides are relishing the new parliamentary term, when news stories come along at a faster rate and so are less likely to linger in the headlines.

After the initial flip-flopping on whether the government would be able to exempt more prisoners, the mother of PC Harper told BBC Breakfast that the handling of the situation had been a "hash".

Government officials working on the plans have spoken to the families of victims, who made it clear they did not want the new measures to be dripped out in leaks to the media.

Instead it was decided one big announcement would be the neatest option.

It had seemed likely that would come in the form of a parliamentary statement on Tuesday from the justice secretary.

Instead, the prime minister decided to make the announcement himself in an interview with BBC Breakfast.

It is understood Burnham was mindful of mounting speculation and wanted to give victims and the public as much certainty at the earliest possible opportunity.

In doing so, he may have risked the ire of the Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle, who is generally disdainful of governments that make major announcements outside of Parliament.

He may also have offered up ammunition to the Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, who has already accused Burnham of being a "people pleaser" who finds it difficult to say no to people.

That characterisation is likely to be tested again when more stories inevitably appear about the victims of prisoners who will still be released early.

It already started on Sunday morning, when the domestic abuse commissioner said she remained "deeply concerned about the number of abusers" still set to be freed.

While this is not the first time Burnham has said he has pushed the system to the limit, Whitehall sources are now adamant there will be no more additional exemptions.

News.title: Police release one of two fatal fire suspects
News.content:
A 31-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder over a fatal house fire has been released with no further action while a second man, aged 23, continues to be questioned.

Natalie McDonald, 34, died in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of Wednesday, along with her niece Valentina Foster, seven.

Cleveland Police said a 48-year-old woman had been left in a critical condition in hospital and another three people had injuries that were not life-threatening.

The force added enquiries were ongoing.

Natalie's mother, Lisa Kirton, described her as "a beautiful soul, who would have done anything for anybody".

Valentina, who was known as Tina, was staying at the house for the summer holidays and had been "dancing around the living room" only the previous night.

"She was a cute little kid," Kirton said. "I can't believe it, seven years old - it's just a disgrace."

In an update on Friday afternoon, Cleveland Police ACC Dave Sutherland said the force was not currently linking the fire to a crash on the A66, in which seven people died, including two police officers.

News.title: Church leads tributes for man killed at festival
News.content:
The man killed at a Christian festival in West Sussex on Friday has been named by his church as Robert Guanco, 41.

He was a pastor at Jesus the Living Water Church in Eastbourne, East Sussex.

Six other people were injured at the event by a falling sign at the Big Church Festival, near Steyning, four of whom were taken to hospital for treatment.

In a statement, his church said: "Pastor Robert was a faithful servant of God, a loving husband to Isay, a devoted and caring father to Ellie, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched. His life, his faith, his love, and his service to God will never be forgotten."

On a fundraising page for Guanco's family, pastor Norman Ponce from Jesus the Living Water Worldwide Church, said he was a "faithful servant of God".

"What was meant to be a time of worship, fellowship, and celebration became an unimaginable tragedy," he added.

Ponce said Guanco was a "beloved son, cherished brother, loving husband" and "great father".

"He was also a good friend, mentor, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched," Ponce said.

"His life reflected humility, faith, love, compassion, and service. Through his ministry, kindness, prayers, and encouragement, he touched many lives."

News.title: Two missing as French trawler sinks in Channel
News.content:
Searches for two crew members from a French fishing boat which sank in the English Channel have been suspended after a second day, the Maritime and Coastguard Agency has said.

A coastguard rescue helicopter, fixed-wing plane and RNLI lifeboats began searching an area south-west of Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth, Devon, after the five-strong crew of the trawler the Maranello made a distress call at 18:00 BST on Saturday.

The intensive multi-agency search continued on Sunday before it was "suspended pending further information", coastguards said at 20:20 on Sunday.

HM Coastguard said three people rescued from the boat and taken to hospital were "currently travelling back to France".

The French authorities said the stricken fishing vessel had contacted another trawler, the Stradale, to say it had a problem with its fishing gear.

The Stradale managed to recover three of the five crew members before the Maranello sank, the French naval prefecture for the Atlantic added.

One of the rescued sailors was evacuated by helicopter and treated in hospital in Truro, Cornwall, while the other two were taken to Plymouth for medical attention.

RNLI lifeboat crews from Falmouth and Newlyn in Cornwall, as well as from Plymouth and Salcombe in Devon, have been involved in the operation.

A large number of civilian vessels had also assisted in the "intensive search" for the two remaining crew members, a UK coastguard spokesperson added.

They said a coastguard aircraft "equipped with the latest technology including a multi-function search radar and high resolution cameras" was also involved, and that mayday relay broadcasts had been sent out, "requesting vessels in the area to keep a sharp lookout."

News.title: Attack mum's trauma of fighting early release plan
News.content:
Reacting to the announcement, Emma Webber said: "I'm glad it has happened, it is the right thing.

"But I'll tell you what wasn't the right thing, the trauma of victims, who have been through so much already, have had to go through to fight for this.

"Petitions, doing news interviews, having to talk about the terrible losses we have suffered and there are dozens of us that have had to do this.

"I try not to be always confrontational and always fighting but as much as I try not to, it seems to be the only way that things are getting done.

"Everything we have done as families in the Nottingham attacks has come at such great cost and yes we are getting results but we shouldn't have had to do any of it at all."

She said the controversy reflected wider problems with funding across the justice system.

"The fact that we were even having to consider releasing people who had taken lives and destroyed families and communities early from their sentences is abhorrent.

"I stand by what I said yesterday - it is morally bankrupt."

She also confirmed after making a call to meet ministers some weeks ago, they had now received an invitation to meet with Justice Secretary Alex Norris, where their concerns would be raised.

News.title: Third murder charge over Brent Council HQ stabbing
News.content:
A total of three people have now been charged with murder over the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley.

David Wynter died after he was attacked on Engineers Way at about 14:30 BST on 25 August.

A 15-year-old boy was charged with murder two days later, and two more teenagers - a 17-year-old boy and 18-year-old Jahquarn St Hillaire - were charged with murder and possession of an offensive weapon on Saturday.

The 15-year-old was remanded in custody and is due to appear at the Old Bailey on 24 September, with the other pair due at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Monday.

News.title: Dementia patient's deportation from Sweden delayed
News.content:
A man with dementia will be able to remain in Sweden while a legal bid to delay his deportation is considered.

The Swedish authorities said they wanted George Mason, originally from Hinckley in Leicestershire, to leave the country by midnight on 20 August, after his application for permanent residency was rejected.

Mason's daughter, Michelle Torossian, said the family had been told an injunction to halt his deportation would be decided by Swedish authorities in a timeframe of two weeks to six months.

Torossian said she was told by the British Embassy in Stockholm that the original deportation decision would not be enforced by the authorities while the injunction order was considered.

The BBC has contacted the Swedish Migration Agency, which said it was unable to comment on individual cases.

News.title: Lola Young surprises Reading Festival with final day set
News.content:
Fans at the final day of Reading Festival were treated to a surprise set from singer Lola Young.

"I am backstage, the cat is out of the bag and I am going to be performing so see you... at the Grid stage," she teased on Instagram, before treating fans to hits including number one single Messy and One Thing.

Her performance marks the latest step in a return to the spotlight after she had to cancel a string of shows last year following an on-stage collapse in September.

Young also pulled out of the 2025 Reading festival due to a scheduling clash.

The weekend festival concludes on Sunday with a line-up including performances by drum and bass duo Chase & Status, and Florence + The Machine.

After Charli XCX ushered in her own new era with an electrifying set following her latest release Music, Fashion, Film, Young's return was welcomed by festival-goers in Reading on Sunday.

Young had cancelled her scheduled appearance at Reading Festival last year due to an "unavoidable scheduling conflict".

A month later, Young dropped her microphone, collapsed backwards and had to be helped off stage in front of a festival crowd in New York.

A few days later, she cancelled all shows "for the foreseeable future".

"I really hope you'll give me a second chance once I've had some time to work on myself and come back stronger," she posted in a message to fans at the time.

Young has sought treatment for drug dependency and told the Guardian, external in 2025 that addiction had dogged her for "a long time".

The pop star has since returned to performing with a small run of shows in the UK, starting with a London gig in March.

"It felt so right being back on stage," she wrote on social media shortly after, but said: "As tempting as it is to jump on a big tour I'm going to continue taking things slowly despite feeling so ready to perform more."

Before touching down in Reading, Young performed at the Electric Picnic Festival in the Republic of Ireland on Saturday.

Although she has returned to performing and released reflective single From Down Here in May this year, fans are still awaiting a fourth album.

Reading Festival winds down on Sunday night with a star-studded cast including indie icon Florence and the Machine, R&B hit-maker Loyle Carner, and Irish rap group Kneecap.

The festival's other site in Leeds, meanwhile, closes after performances from singer-songwriter Raye and multi award-winning rapper Dave on Sunday night.

The U.S. military attacked Iranian rocket launchers positioned in the Strait of Hormuz, marking its first offensive operation in a month, a U.S. official told The Associated Press on Sunday.

Explosions were heard near Larak Island, which lies in the waterway, Iranian media outlets reported.

Iranian forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying mines into the strait, the unnamed U.S. official said. The waterway, a vital trade route, has emerged as a major flash point in the war.

Last week, the U.S. completed an operation to clear mines from strait’s shipping lanes. Following the operation, President Donald Trump warned Iran that “any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed.”

In response to the new offensive, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement that the U.S. attack “will be answered by the sons of Iran and will result in the punishment of the aggressor,” Axios reported.

open image in gallery The US military attacked Iranian rocket launchers positioned in the Strait of Hormuz, marking its first offensive operation in a month, a US official told The Associated Press on Sunday ( Getty Images )

When reached for comment, a Pentagon spokesperson referred The Independent to U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. operations in the Middle East.

The war, which began in February when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran, had largely settled into a stalemate in recent weeks with no clear end in sight.

The strait, which carried about 20 percent of the world’s oil before the conflict, has remained a central obstacle. The U.S. insists it must remain open to unrestricted shipping, while Iran says it has the right to manage traffic through the waterway.

open image in gallery Eighteen US service members have been killed and hundreds more wounded in the conflict, the Pentagon has said ( AFP via Getty Images )

In recent months, the Trump administration has maintained that Iran’s military and leadership have been severely weakened.

“We’ve wiped them out militarily,” Trump said in an interview earlier this month. “The navy’s gone, the air force is gone, the leadership is gone.” He said the deaths of Iranian leaders had also complicated diplomacy because “nobody knows who’s leading.”

Thousands of U.S. strikes have been carried out across the country, sometimes continuing night after night. In Iran, 3,375 people have died and more than 30,000 have been injured, according to the World Health Organization.

The conflict has also taken a significant toll on the United States.

Eighteen U.S. service members have been killed and hundreds more wounded in the conflict, the Pentagon has said. Last month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Congress that the war had cost $37.5 billion. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has also driven up fuel prices.

Multiple recent polls indicate the war is broadly unpopular in the U.S. In a Reuters survey last month, 69 percent of respondents said that Trump has not clearly explained the goals of the conflict.

Fifteen people remained unaccounted for after dozens of people were rescued following a “significant flash food” in the Grand Canyon, according to park officials.

Flash flooding inundated Bright Angel Canyon, a popular hiking trail, and Phantom Ranch areas of the park starting around 2:30 p.m. Saturday.

“These were individuals either on a backcountry itinerary in the inner canyon or believed to be day hiking along the North Kaibab/Phantom Ranch area,” Grand Canyon National Park spokesperson Joelle Baird, a spokeswoman told The New York Times.

On Sunday morning, two helicopters from the National Park Service and Arizona Department of Public Safety searched the North Kaibab Trail and Colorado River from the mouth of Bright Angel Creek to Deer Creek Narrows, though no missing people were found on those flights.

The National Park Service initially said 20 or more people were missing or unaccounted for but later revised its count.

open image in gallery Fifteen people remain unaccounted for after flash flooding in Grand Canyon National Park on August 28 ( NPS Photo/J. Thompson )

As of Sunday morning, 62 people had been evacuated from Phantom Ranch and the lower North Kaibab Trail, the National Park Service said in a previous statement,

More evacuations were scheduled from Cottonwood Campground and Phantom Ranch.

“The NPS is conducting an air evacuation of approximately 50 individuals from the Phantom Ranch area,” an active NPS alert reads.

The flooding also knocked out the sole water pipeline serving the park.

“The flooding caused extensive damage to infrastructure in the inner canyon, including the Transcanyon Waterline, which supplies water from the canyon for use in the park,” the National Park Service said in a statement. “The waterline is currently not operational, leaving the park with limited water reserves and requiring significant water conservation measures to ensure available supplies can be maintained.”

The damage prompted organizers to cease overnight hotel accommodations beginning on Monday and order dry camping across the park.

A flood watch has been issued in the park through the end of the day Monday. Showers and thunderstorms are expected to develop throughout Sunday afternoon and evening, with conditions expected to worsen overnight into Monday.

“Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas,” the Park Service said. “Raging killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.”

open image in gallery A flood watch has been issued through the end of August 31, with showers and thunderstorms expected the next two days ( Parth Desai )

The entirety of the North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch, and Silver and Black Bridges are closed until further notice.

“There is currently no estimated reopening date for these areas and other inner canyon closures may be necessary,” the Park Service said in a statement to The Washington Post.

The Colorado River is also closed due to debris.

Prior to the flooding, three hikers died from extreme heat in the canyon in June.

Phantom Ranch is a historic lodge in the Grand Canyon National Park near the bottom of the Grand Canyon by Bright Angel Creek.

The flash floods totaled one-quarter to three-quarters of an inch in 30 minutes, the National Weather Service said.

The rain caused flooding in and around the Bright Angel Creek Basin below the Dragon Bravo Fire scar, the weather service added. Heavy creek flow was ongoing as a result.

The American Red Cross also opened a shelter at Grand Canyon High School in Grand Canyon Village.

Cameron Norrie will have to console himself with a win at a padel tournament after his miserable summer at the grand slams ended in another first-round defeat.

Norrie, who did not make it past the opening round at the French Open or Wimbledon, was dumped out of the US Open by unheralded Frenchman Luca Van Assche.

It was a sorry Sunday for the 31-year-old, who woke up to find he had been overtaken as British number one by Arthur Fery following his run to the Winston-Salem final.

open image in gallery Norrie took the first set but went on to lose (AP Photo/Andres Kudacki) ( AP )

Norrie revealed beforehand that he won a padel competition among his friends while on his stag do in Ibiza last month.

It turns out that was the only victory he could savour after slipping to a 6-7 (6) 6-2 6-2 6-3 defeat.

Norrie pointedly shouted ‘allez’ on his way to securing a grind of a first set on a tie-break.

Whether that wound up Van Assche is unclear but the 22-year-old made no such mistake in the second to haul himself level.

Norrie, the 29th seed, then found himself in a New York nightmare as the match quickly got away from him.

open image in gallery Norrie was beaten by Luca van Assche (Andres Kudacki/AP) ( AP )

“It was really tough,” he said. “I was pretty nervous and it showed in the beginning of the first set, and I did well to steal that first set.

“But I could never really maintain a good level of energy and momentum, and I’d play well for a little bit and then drop off a couple of games here and there.

“So that was super frustrating and pretty surprising. I felt like I lost to myself today.”

There was better news for Britain in the women’s draw as Katie Boulter came through a tough match against American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee.

British number one Boulter, 30, looked to be cruising through at a set and a break ahead, only for some costly double-faults to let Lee back in.

However, Boulter, cheered on by new husband Alex De Minaur, gathered herself on a noisy, partisan Court Five to win 6-4 3-6 6-0.

“You know, I expected a battle in the first round,” said Boulter. “I don’t think that there’s any match out here that’s straightforward, really.

“I think I did well to get over the line in the first set, and then I think I changed a couple of things that actually made a huge difference in the third. So I was really pleased with that in the third set.”

A tricky assignment could await in round two with a potential tie against this year’s Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova.

British number four Jacob Fearnley was a break down in the first set against Spain’s Martin Landaluce when play was suspended for rain.

Following a weekend trip to his Virginia golf club, President Donald Trump jumped on his Truth Social account to sound off on one his favorite topics: his anger around the state of his signature construction projects to renovate the Kennedy Center and the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

“Kennedy Center is an old and decrepit building that is badly in need of a major construction and public relations fix before it can attain greatness and prestige, perhaps far greater than ever before,” the president wrote in one post on Sunday night. “It has been losing a fortune for many years, and will continue to do so if the highly conflicted judge on the case doesn’t allow us to do what has to be done!”

A federal judge will determine whether the Trump-dominated Kennedy Center board violated court orders by approving an inscription to the building that it has been “renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump.” The board voted for the change despite a court ruling in May that the performing arts venue cannot be renamed without congressional approval.

Lawyers for Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex officio Kennedy Center board member, argued this week the new plan is an end-run around the May decision and a “breathtaking assault on the rule of law” meant to cover for the financial chaos caused by the president’s takeover, which has prompted a string of artist cancelations and a reported slowdown in ticket sales.

The Trump administration, meanwhile, argues the building is in dire need of renovation, to the point that it could someday need to be torn down unless the build plan moves forward.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump sounded off on Truth Social on August 30 about his ongoing attempt to rename the Kennedy Center and renovate the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ( Getty )

“The concept of, if the building is not properly renovated and restored, eventually it falls into a state of disrepair and it cannot be used,” Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said outside the court on Thursday. “It’ll just run out of money … and over time it’ll just go down and down and down, until at some point, a building that was built in 1964 that isn't renovated does eventually get torn down.”

The president’s projects on the National Mall, meanwhile, have been no less fraught, as Trump acknowledged in his Sunday posting spree.

“Look what VANDALS did to the grass connecting the vandalized World War II Monument and the vandalized Reflecting Pool, which will be opened again, and better than ever, shortly,” he wrote. “Anybody who thinks the Reflecting Pool wasn’t vandalized should go back to Law School!”

He posted an image that appeared to show “86 47” in the lawn.

“The grass is being replaced shortly, and the Reflecting Pool is almost completely fixed, including the various inflow and outflow pipes, which we were saving for the end of the year, but will do now,” he added.

open image in gallery The Reflecting Pool is still not operational, while the Kennedy Center project is locked in a legal battle with a congresswoman challenging the president’s plan to rename the arts complex after himself ( AP )

The president has insisted vandals were behind peels and cracks in the newly refinished Reflecting Pool, which has had to be drained multiple times since the president took over fixing it.

But administration officials have admitted that the damage was likely from poor construction, forcing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro to drop a high-profile case against a former Olympian after finding that the damage was “the result of flawed installation by the contractor.”

The result infuriated Trump, who has openly attacked D.C.’s top prosecutor over the decision.

Earlier this month, Pirro called on the judge overseeing the case to leave open the possibility of new charges against David Hearn, who had pleaded not guilty and denied all wrongdoing prior to the dismissal of charges.

Vandals indeed appeared to target the grass nearby, where the apparent anti-Trump slogan “86 47” was found inscribed in dead grass in July.

The patch of grass was also the site of the president’s Great American State Fair in July, which saw thousands of visitors at the site across two weeks of events.

On Thursday, a woman was indicted on two felony counts for allegedly spray painting another nearby monument, the WWII Memorial.

She is expected to be arraigned next week. A federal judge has aleady rejected Pirro’s attempts to keep her in jail while the legal battle plays out.

Lanterns is really leaning into its mean streak, with a double act unlike any on TV at the moment – and Kyle Chandler has compared his character’s fear of giving up his power to his own status as an actor in his 60s.

The HBO Max show, which is based on of the DC comic book superhero, stars Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan, a grumpy version of the character who has been tasked with training his replacement, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre). The problem is, he really doesn’t want to give up the gig.

In episode three, we learn about how John came to be selected by the Green Lantern Corps. It was actually his father who was originally targeted when John was just a baby, but when he failed to pass the test of bravery, they returned to test John as an adult.

open image in gallery Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler in HBO Max show 'Lanterns' ( HBO Max )

At the end of the episode, after being questioned by an extra-terrestrial Guardian of the Universe (Laura Linney), he is approved to become the next Green Lantern. Only Hal isn’t going to hand over the baton without a fight – and makes that very clear in the episode’s closing moments.

In an interview with The Independent, Chandler said that John’s youth poses “an AI-style threat” to the ego of a man who might not be physically capable of carrying out the role in the near future – something the 60-year-old can associate with in real life as an actor.

“As we were shooting this, the one thing that immediately came to me was, ‘I’m 60 years old and I’m well aware I’ve got another good 10 years of physical activity, another 10 years maybe of I don’t know what – and then you know, you’re sort of hanging up your boots at that point –as me, Kyle. So this character, I saw it immediately like that.”

He continued: “If I was going to step out of acting, I would step out of my identity – it’s been 36 years doing this – and that’s not an easy thing to do; it’s a scary thing to do.

“I see it now with my contemporaries – they’re retiring. If you retire, you lose your friendships at work, you lose your identity – you have to recreate yourself through who you really are and that’s like being born again. I just thought, for Hal, that is not a place he wants to go, so yeah, this young punk is a threat - a big threat. Like an AI threat.”

Chandler said this dynamic opened up “so much area for humour and fun”, with his character constantly “attacking him for being youthful and not having the wisdom I have”. In fact, the actor said the scene in the opening episode, in which he jumps out of the driver’s seat of the car as it heads towards a cliff, leaving John behind as a passenger, was what made him want to sign on the dotted line.

open image in gallery ‘Lanterns’ star Kyle Chandler ( HBO Max )

“The opportunity to, in essence, try to kill him, it would seem – that was fun! The first episode when that car goes where it goes, I laughed so much when I saw that cut. And that’s what got me wanting to do the show to begin with.”

Lanterns – which also stars Kelly Macdonald and Garrett Dilahunt – airs on HBO Max in the UK and US.

On a moonless and rainy night, a group of soldiers emerged from a ramshackle building meant to resemble a church. The alpine terrain loomed over them as they quietly set off for the tree line of the German countryside a short distance away.

The soldiers are members of the Polish special forces and are taking part in an exercise designed only months ago that simulates moving through enemy lines, traversing miles of enemy territory and launching a drone strike on a key enemy location.

Initially designed by the Army's Green Berets for U.S. special forces, the exercise that began Friday is informed by and simulates many of the challenges that Ukrainian troops have experienced in their conflict with Russia. It is the first time a NATO ally like Poland has undertaken the training, and it comes at a time when tensions between Russian President Vladimir Putin and NATO countries have escalated.

“We’re using lessons learned from Ukraine,” an Army Green Beret officer assigned to the training complex said Thursday. “All of those effects that we’re seeing either Russia or Ukraine having to overcome — we’re doing our best to replicate.”

The Associated Press received rare access to both the training ground and the troops conducting the exercise, which has only been conducted twice before, both times this year, by two different Green Beret teams.

The drill highlights the focus that some parts of the U.S. military have on learning the latest techniques in drone warfare, pioneered by Ukraine during its 4 1/2-year effort to repel Russian forces. It also shows how the U.S., its NATO allies and Ukraine are working together to counter the threat of possible further Russian action in coming years even as the Trump administration has warned of troop drawdowns in Europe.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe went to Moscow this week to warn Russia not to attack NATO countries, The Wall Street Journal reported. Russia has the appetite to conduct sabotage and cyberattacks against NATO countries, but Putin wants to avoid a direct confrontation, according to three Western officials, who spoke Friday on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military matters.

How special forces are learning to sneak behind enemy lines to deploy drones

During the exercise in Germany, a senior enlisted soldier familiar with the training scenario at Joint Multinational Readiness Center Hohenfels — about an hour's drive southeast from Nuremberg — said the plan is to run it several times a year. The officer said he expects most, if not all, of the 32 NATO nations to express interest in sending their troops to try the exercise.

Both spoke on condition of anonymity in line with the U.S. military's longstanding policy of not publicly identifying individual members of special forces units.

The scenario, which runs for several days, takes place on a large, 1,100-square-mile (3,000-square-kilometer) plot of land nestled in the Bavarian countryside.

Poland's special forces will be expected to sneak past a U.S. Army airborne infantry unit, whose soldiers will play the enemy. The U.S. airborne infantry unit will parachute into the closed-off training area at the Army's Hohenfels base and set themselves up into a front line.

Assuming the Polish forces can make their way past the U.S. Army, they must then move north — through about 60 miles (100 kilometers) of German countryside — to another training area in the town of Grafenwoehr, where they are expected to destroy a simulated target.

In between lie German farms and villages, private and government cameras, as well as a city with a large population, all of which not only pose as obstacles but also create the potential for them to be spotted.

The senior enlisted soldier said that in previous instances of the exercise, the Army Green Berets removed their uniforms “so they can blend in” before adding that “blend in also means don’t get seen by civilians.”

German civilians in the area largely are not aware of the exercise and serve as a reasonable test of how well special forces can blend into the local population. If they fail, reports of suspicious people to police will make it back to the military, which will use them to pinpoint the team.

“This is supposed to be Russia and you’re going to stand out in Russia,” the enlisted soldier added.

Plus, the U.S. Army also will be looking for the Polish forces with drones of their own.

If they're spotted, “now you have the entire Russian arsenal coming at you,” the enlisted soldier said.

The U.S. Army can either send a military police unit to hunt for the Polish special forces with dogs or direct more drones to the area. In previous versions of the exercise, the U.S. Army had access to more than a hundred drones, the enlisted soldier said.

Troops are able to be “captured or killed” as part of the training.

Countries seek help from Ukraine on drone warfare

While the exercise taps into drones and NATO teamwork, the message of collaboration and the value of drones has been somewhat mixed lately across the military.

President Donald Trump stirred confusion among NATO allies by going back and forth on drawing down U.S. troop levels in Europe, and the administration has launched a force review on next steps. And last week, the Army’s top officer shuttered a unit that specialized in drone warfare.

But overall, there is growing interest in tapping Ukraine for its expertise on modern warfare and, specifically, drones.

In March, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was helping five countries in the Middle East and Gulf region counter Iranian drone attacks launched during the war with the United States, while the U.S. and European countries were among those requesting support.

Meanwhile, the number of mysterious drone incursions in Europe have grown, including as recently as this month, when a pair of drones were spotted over a German military base and a drone carrying explosives was found at a key cargo airport in Germany.

___

Associated Press writer Emma Burrows in London contributed to this report.

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season, then?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick amidst another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Sports.title: Fresh misery for dropped Chelsea keeper Robert Sanchez as it’s revealed he was fined for speeding on motorway
Sports.content:
AXED Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sánchez was caught speeding by a motorway camera, it has been revealed.

The £25million ace, 28, was doing 47mph in a 40mph zone on the M23 in Crawley, Surrey.



Spaniard Sánchez was convicted of speeding and slapped with three licence penalty points.

The player, said to earn £60,000 a week, was also fined £1,520 for the offence last October.



Crawley magistrates’ court dealt with the case in April but it has only just been disclosed in public records, obtained by The Sun.

It came amid concerns over his position as the Blues’ No1 goalie.



He was dropped for yesterday’s match against Brighton after Chelsea signed ­Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

Sánchez arrived at Stamford Bridge from Brighton in 2023.

Sánchez remained Chelsea’s No 1 despite a woeful start against Fulham following two mistakes in Chelsea’s 3-2 win.

No keeper has made more mistakes leading to shots since the start of the 2024/25 season than the Spaniard.



Sánchez’s fine includes a £1,000 financial penalty, a £400 victim surcharge, and £120 court costs.

Sports.title: ‘Best for the team’ – Xabi Alonso tight-lipped over Enzo Fernandez after Chelsea star axed but still no Man City bid
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are prepared for any eventuality after Enzo Fernandez was left out of another squad, with the Blues braced for a double departure.

Fernandez, 25, is pushing for a move to Manchester City before Tuesday’s transfer deadline and has been absent from the last two matchday squads.



Alonso, who made it two Premier League wins from two as Chelsea boss, could not guarantee £100million-rated Pedro Neto, who started and scored against Brighton, would remain at the club.

City are yet to make their first official bid for Fernandez, valued at more than £120m by Chelsea. City are expected to lodge a first bid of around £100m.



Asked if Fernandez had played his final game for the club, Alonso said: “We’ll see.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we made the decision against Luton and today and anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.



“We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Neto, 26, was in talks over a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal before Chelsea’s asking price put them off and they turned their attention to Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli.

The Portugal international has been involved in all three games under Alonso so far this season and scored his first goal of the season against the Seagulls.

But Alonso declined to say that he would be staying at the club.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Spaniard said: “No, in football I don’t guarantee anything, not anyone.

“But I was very happy with Pedro. He did really well, he played with a lot of energy.

“He is going to be very important for the team for the whole season because he has different special qualities.

“He is a threat in one-v-one, he attacks very well in the space, he is strong, he is competitive.



“I am happy that he scored, he was really close to scoring another one. I am very happy with Pedro.”

Romeo Lavia, Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer were also on the scoresheet in Chelsea’s 4-3 win over Brighton.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola could be £123million mistake for Liverpool… Reds need midfield steel not more flashy wingers
Sports.content:
SOMEONE’S been asleep at the wheel inside Anfield, or the recruitment team led by Richard Hughes is simply blind.

Liverpool’s lack of midfield defensive cover was there for all to see last season.



Glaring holes for the opposition to run through, a lack of bite in the tackle, a naive belief that the attack-minded pair of Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister could somehow alter their footballing DNA and become dogs of war.

Fast forward to Andoni Iraola’s first home game in charge and it was groundhog day — Nottingham Forest’s quick counter-attacks causing mayhem, Szoboszlai and Mac Allister headless chickens without the ball.



There is joy that sporting director Hughes has finally agreed a transfer fee worth up to £123million with Paris Saint-Germain for Bradley Barcola, who is set to sign on within the next 24 hours on £300,000 a week.

But for all that he is a star attraction, the Frenchman also happens to be a winger.



Rocket science would not be required to work out someone of Barcola’s exciting talent might step up as a marquee successor to departed Mo Salah.

Yet over three months of haggling with the Champions League holders in desperate pursuit of the 23-year-old, a critical weakness was somehow completely ignored.

And the obsession with Barcola could turn into a fatal attraction.

For Oliver Glasner’s side, just like Newcastle did on the opening weekend of the season, ran right through Iraola’s malfunctioning engine room.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Dan Ndoye scored one goal and could have had three, while in the first half Igor Jesus almost had the run of the Liverpool box thanks to precise and pacey passing from behind.

True, Kop ace Florian Wirtz was denied a goal by the tightest of offside margins soon after Ndoye had opened the scoring, having already missed two chances.

But seconds before the break, with chaos all around him, Reds keeper Alisson had to be world class to deny Jesus — and at 2-0 then that would surely have been game over.

The need for someone to get down and dirty, to practice the dark arts and do almost anything to protect the back four is so glaringly clear it is almost laughable.



Yet with the transfer window about to shut nobody with such traits has been brought in.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard — no stranger to a biting tackle or a red card in his day — got it in a nutshell.

He stressed of the Iraola side that has now twice had to fire-fight its way to 2-2 draws under him: “They are too nice.

“They’ve got a load of nice technical players but they lack that little bit of nastiness. All over the pitch they have to be more at it, taking yellow cards if they need to. That’s the problem Iraola faces — you need some nastiness, you can’t be so nice.”



At least Victor Munoz, the same age but at around a quarter of Barcola’s price from Osasuna, has a bit about him.

The Spanish World Cup winner’s turn and fierce shot for Liverpool’s second leveller on 82 minutes spoke of a selfless grafter.

But Iraola is overseeing a collection of individuals, not a team, and there is nobody in the middle galvanising them.

Wirtz does look too ‘nice’ and so does the second of last summer’s £100m-plus arrivals, Alexander Isak.



The Swede tapped home the first equaliser but lacks the physicality of a scrapper.

It may well be nice to have Barcola alongside him and Wirtz but if there is no ball-winner, no destroyer, then like the other two so far he could just become another fashion accessory.

Iraola was right to complain that the three minutes of delay as bungling fourth official Tim Robinson fumbled with his subs board with Rio Ngumoha, Ryan Gravenberch and Kostas Tsimikas waiting to go on, gave Forest a window of opportunity.

Yet £50m new boy Liam Delap’s quickly taken throw that ended in a dodgy penalty decision for Neco Williams — with Morgan Gibbs-White converting — once again said it all about lack of cover.

Glasner, hoping to welcome his Crystal Palace old boy Daniel Munoz into the Forest fold, should and could have been celebrating his first win as the new boss.

Iraola is also still without a victory — but crucially still minus a midfield scrapper.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham praises Jose Mourinho for releasing shackles & giving him ‘freedom’ after red-hot start to Real season
Sports.content:
JUDE BELLINGHAM was Real Madrid’s ‘free lion’ as last season’s crisis club extended their rip-roaring start under Jose Mourinho.

England star Bellingham scored the first and saw another effort put down as an own goal in a mauling of Malaga.



It is three wins in three LaLiga games in the Special One’s second coming as manager at the Bernabeu.

Real — left for dead by Barcelona last term under both Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa — have scored 10 goals so far and conceded just two.



Bellingham has been a big part of that and explained why — Mourinho has given him licence to roam.

The Brummie, now fluent in Spanish, said: “I feel more free now. I have more freedom to move, to go up and down the pitch depending on what we need.

“I’m really enjoying my football — and that’s why I’m performing well.”

Kylian Mbappe, scorer of a hat-trick against Real Sociedad on Wednesday, added a third with just half an hour on the clock. And Arda Guler came off the bench to make it four late on.

Bellingham netted first on 19 minutes with a superb solo effort. He out-muscled Angel Recio in the middle of the park before driving at pace into the box.

That left two other challengers trailing before he fired home from a tight angle on the right.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

VAR refused to uphold Recio’s cries of foul — and Real were on their way.

Bellingham was unlucky not to claim his side’s second after Mbappe saw a shot parried.

He leapt to head the rebound goalwards but defender Carlos Puga ended up whacking it over the line off keeper Alfonso Herrero.

England reject Trent Alexander-Arnold had been brought back for this one and provided a pinpoint cross from the right four minutes later for Mbappe to convert first time.



It was a 60th LaLiga goal for the France superstar. Only Harry Kane has been scoring more in Europe’s top leagues since Mbappe left Paris Saint-Germain in 2024.

The second half was less impressive. Bernardo Silva came off the bench and so did Guler after Malaga had a penalty award overturned by VAR.

Guler tapped home Vinicius Junior’s cross from point-blank range following a swift one-two with the Brazilian.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals he’s ‘BEGGING’ Premier League chiefs to make major rule change to overhaul matchday squads
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA has been “begging” Premier League officials to expand matchday squads for the “welfare of the players”.

Rules currently allow managers to name nine substitutes on the bench, an increase from the seven permitted before the Covid-19 pandemic.



But Arteta wants Prem chiefs to increase that so he does not have to leave anyone at home.

The Arsenal boss, whose side go to Aston Villa tonight, has had to leave stars like Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus out of his matchday squad this term and feels it leads to a number of issues — that duo are now both set to leave.



Arteta said: “That’s why I have been begging the Premier League to extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing.

“I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have.

“But these are the rules, and within the rules, we have to play.

“We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

The Gunners chief revealed last week that Gabriel Jesus was not part of Arsenal training because of the “numbers in the squad”.

And Arteta does not want to continue having “tough” conversations with players who would rather be with the squad than at home watching on TV.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He added: “More than anybody, the question has to be to the players.

“What do they want? If they say, ‘no, I prefer to stay at home’, then we have an issue because then they don’t love what they do.

“But I’m sure if you ask players, everybody would like to be part of the squad on matchday.

“Otherwise, you have to tell someone they aren’t even part of the matchday squad. That’s really, really tough. And it doesn’t help anybody.

“It doesn’t help the club, doesn’t help the valuation of the player and doesn’t help them to feel part of it.



“In my opinion, it is a real issue with a really, really simple solution.”

Sports.title: Mario Balotelli slams ‘phones & PlayStations’ for ‘ruining’ football and reveals advice he’d tell his 16-year-old self
Sports.content:
MARIO Balotelli has slammed the impact of mobile phones and video games on football.

The 36-year-old explained that the current crop of young stars coming through have experienced a vastly different upbringing to himself.



Balotelli has noted that he no longer sees young children playing football in the streets in Italy, like when he was a youngster.

He has suggested that modern mobile phone and video game culture is to blame for this shift in entertainment.



The Italian star told The Guardian that the shift now sees young footballers playing less football than previous generations.

Balotelli said: “Computers, phones, and PlayStations have ruined a lot.



“Above all, the parents’ mentality has changed. A seven‑year-old kid today might play football for two hours every three days.

“We had the same structured training sessions, plus three hours of playing at the park every day, which felt like fun but was actually extra training.

“I truly believe talents were born on the street and in the parks.”

He explained that playing against older children helped to raise his game in a way that is less common in the modern age.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The striker claimed that “it’s very different” because he would learn skills on the streets, rather than just watching videos online.

This upbringing seemed to serve Balotelli well as he went on to score 14 goals in 36 caps for Italy between 2010 and 2018.

Even 20 years after coming through at Lumezzane, Balotelli is continuing to ply his trade professionally for Al-Ittifaq in the UAE First Division.

But it has not been a straight-forward career for the controversial star.

Former Scotland midfielder Scott Brown, 41, even recalled being threatened on the pitch by the striker during a game.



Balotelli’s wild side even threatened to re-emerge after falling out of favour at Genoa last year.

But the Italian has explained that there are lessons he wished he could tell his 16-year-old self.

Balotelli continued: “I’d tell him not to make certain choices and to listen to certain people at specific times.”
