Fabio Vieira is set to complete a permanent move to Hamburg after spending last season on loan at the German side, with the Arsenal midfielder undergoing a medical as HSV board member Kathleen Kruger confirms transfer talks took place in London

Arsenal midfielder Fabio Vieira looks set to follow Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus out of the Emirates Stadium exit as he closes in on a £7m move. The 26-year-old is completing the formalities over a permanent move to Bundesliga side Hamburger SV, where he spent last season on loan.

‌



With days until the transfer window closes, Andrea Berta is culling the fringe players in North London ahead of the market closure on September 1. Vieira is set to make the move to Germany with HSV on the verge of winning the race for the Portuguese's signature.

‌



But his move comes amid the backdrop of an exodus at the Premier League champions with Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli on the brink of completing departures.

Sports.title: Liverpool set to complete transfer before deadline with clever clause agreed
Sports.content:
Liverpool set to complete transfer before deadline with clever clause agreed

Liverpool's Stefan Bajcetic is closing in on the exit door after falling down the Anfield pecking order but, despite preparing for a return to Celta Vigo, the Reds have kept the door open to a move

View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic is closing in on a Liverpool exit

Liverpool are ready to sanction Stefan Bajcetic's exit with the midfielder closing in on a return to Celta Vigo.

‌



The 21-year-old began his career with the Spanish side before moving to Anfield, but after impressing initially back when Jurgen Klopp was in charge Bajcetic has endured an injury-hit few years and is no longer part of the plans on Merseyside.

‌



Talk of Bajcetic heading back to Celta Vigo has been ongoing for weeks and a move is expected to materialise before Tuesday's deadline. A transfer fee remains a subject of discussion but Liverpool are expected to include a buy-back clause, reports the Athletic.

‌



Bajcetic's Liverpool contract is due to expire at the end of this season and he has not made a appearance for the club since May 2024. He last played a competitive game in May 2025 during a loan spell with Las Palmas.

Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford's impact on Man Utd transfer deadline day plan as 'new signing' hailed

Marcus Rashford's reintegration into the Manchester United starting picture has given Michael Carrick less reason to make any late transfer moves

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has returned to Man Utd to give them even more attacking depth

Michael Carrick admitted Marcus Rashford’s return to the Manchester United starting line-up has eased the need for last-minute business in the transfer window.

‌



Carrick gave Rashford his first United start in 626 days and while he did not get on the scoresheet in the 5-2 win over Ipswich at Old Trafford, the 28-year-old England attacker impressed his manager.

‌



And Rashford’s return to United’s squad has clearly influenced their transfer window policy. With the clock ticking down to the window’s close, Carrick said: “I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with.

‌



“I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team, you know. Adding Marcus into that feels like a new signing. So, in that respect, we're quite happy.”

Carrick, though, did not rule out any eleventh hour deals. He went on: “It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left. I think the situation that we're in. We're always open to if there's something else to be able to add, so I wouldn't shut that down, but as it stands, we'll have to wait and see.”

Sports.title: Brilliant Bruno Fernandes and VAR loophole help Man Utd thrash Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Brilliant Bruno Fernandes and VAR loophole help Man Utd thrash Ipswich - 5 talking points

MANCHESTER UNITED 5-2 IPSWICH TOWN: Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as the hosts overcame going behind to secure a comfortable three points

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspired Man Utd to three points

Manchester United came from behind to down Ipswich and secure their first Premier League win of the season thanks to a Bruno Fernandes hat-trick - but the win wasn't without its controversy.

‌



Leif Davis shocked the Stretford End when he put Ipswich ahead on 29 minutes before the host drew themselves level thanks to talisman Fernandes, who was sent clear after a defensive mishap.

‌



Jacob Greaves put through his own net to put United ahead for the first time, but only after Harry Maguire had handled the ball before receiving a VAR reprieve.

‌



Fernandes was on hand to score from 12 yards to give Michael Carrick's side a two-goal cushion on the hour mark before he bagged his third United treble thanks a fortuitous bounce that allowed him to score from close range. Bryan Mbuemo completed the rout before Chuba Akpom scored a consolation in stoppage time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The visitors, who once lost this fixture 9-0 back in the 1990s, were certainly don't going to allow a repeat. Julio Enciso showcased immense pace to race onto a long ball before Senne Lammens denied him. The Belgian was beaten though when Davis put the Tractor Boys ahead.

‌



Abdul Fatawu squared up and beat Luke Shaw before firing in his cross, which the Ipswich left-back met first time with his shot cannoning in off the crossbar to silence Old Trafford.

United, as they have done regularly in recent years, needed their PFA Player of the Year to haul them out of trouble. An Ipswich error left the hosts two-on-one and Fernandes was sent clear by Matheus Cunha, before hammering past Kjell Scherpen.

View 5 Images Harry Maguire's goal opened the floodgates for the Red Devils

‌



The Red Devils missed the chance to put themselves ahead early in the second-half when Bryan Mbuemo somehow hit the bar from a yard out, but Maguire soon had them ahead in controversial circumstances which will go down as a Greaves own goal.

United firmly took control of the contest when Fernandes scored his second from the spot after Cunha had been fouled. He would complete his hat-trick before Mbeumo got on the scoresheet to add further gloss to the result.

Here's five talking points from Old Trafford.

‌



Bruno untouchable

Having just been named the Premier League's best player off the back of what he did last season, where he broke record for assists in a single campaign, Fernandes is clearly flowing with confidence at an all-time high.

Gary Neville remarked on commentary that the Portuguese playmaker is the best signing of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era and few could disagree. In fact it is almost impossible to disagree. Fernandes was United's talisman last season and, even with the quality around him, that status doesn't look like changing.

Maguire controversy

Never will the England defender be so glad to see a shot be heading wide, but the influence of VAR and the laws they can intervene on will be under serious scrutiny after United's second goal, which put them in charge of the contest.

‌



View 5 Images A controversial explanation saw Man Utd's second goal stand

Maguire clearly handled the ball seconds before he took his shot, but as his effort was going wide and deflected in by Greaves, it meant his actions weren't under the microscope as the goalscorer. Had he scored then we may have had a different outcome - and that will not sit well with many.

Ipswich collapse after positive hour

The last time Ipswich were in the top flight under Kieran McKenna it was off the back of successive promotions and the Tractor Boys ultimately won just four games and finished 16 points from safety. Their squad looked that bit short, but this time round they've got several of the players who will be better off for that experience.

‌



They've also got the likes of Daizen Maeda, signed from Celtic, and several individuals who've impressed in the Premier League previously, Issa Diop among them. Gary O'Neil has top flight experience as a manager.

View 5 Images Bruno Fernandes' first of the afternoon got Man Utd level

Crazy to think that you could take any positives from such a hammering defeat, but for an hour Ipswich were in this game and it needed a controversial moment before the floodgates opened. O'Neil needs to see the first 60 minutes as a blueprint for the season.

‌



Where is Sesko at?

Last season started slow and then he became known as a super sub, coming off the bench to win numerous games once United hit form. But heading into his second season the Slovenian will surely have felt he'd done enough to begin establishing himself in the first XI.

Instead he began on the bench for a second week in succession. His introduction came late against Hull and this weekend he was only given 11 minutes by Carrick. If Sesko was hoping to kick on, his plans are certainly on hold.

View 5 Images Leif Davis had given Ipswich a first-half lead

‌



Rashford's revival

Few would've thought that it would only take Rashford one game of the Premier League season before he was back starting games for United again. Their attack was purring last season under Carrick without him and there didn't seem to be any great clamour for him to return.

But a lot can change in a short space of time and Rashford was called upon at half-time against Hull last weekend, even if he couldn't turn the tide the day. Nevertheless he did enough to convince his boss that he was worthy of a start as his secondcoming at his boyhood club continues.

Sports.title: Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball
Sports.content:
Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand after an initial VAR check as Harry Maguire's shot found the bottom corner

View 2 Images Harry Maguire's goal for Manchester United against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand despite a handball in the build up

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand despite the ball hitting Harry Maguire's HAND in the build-up.

‌



Maguire, 33, fired United into a 2-1 lead in the 57th minute at Old Trafford after controlling the ball on the edge of the box before drilling a low shot that was deflected home by Jacob Greaves for an own goal.

‌



However, the ball appeared to hit Maguire's hand when he won it back, leaving the Ipswich players incensed that the goal should be disallowed. But, because he was not the actual goalscorer, the goal is allowed to stand.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

If Maguire had directly benefited from the handball and been the scorer, a free-kick would have awarded to Ipswich. As he was not, United were given a second goal and took the lead for the first time in the game.

"The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball," the Premier League said.

‌



VAR added: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

Gary Neville delivered his verdict on the incident and repeated what was said by VAR when they were discussing about disallowing the goal. "If that shot had been on target it wouldn't have been a goal," Neville told Sky Sports.

View 2 Images Harry Maguire puts Manchester United ahead against Ipswich Town (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"VAR say to the referee 'hear me out and listen to me' because they know it's going to be complicated."

United had fallen behind in the 29th minute as Ipswich took a shock lead. Abdul Fatawu went past Luke Shaw with ease on the right-hand side before pulling the ball back for Leif Davis to smash home.

But the Reds responded 11 minutes later as Matheus Cunha pounced on an error from Marcelino Nunez to slide a pass through to Bruno Fernandes and he did the rest, slotting the ball beyond the Ipswich goalkeeper.

‌



Although Ipswich hadmade a bright start to the second half, United were ruthless in attack. After Greaves' own-goal put them ahead, Fernandes scored from the spot soon after to make it 3-1 to the Reds.

Fernandes wrapped up his hat-trick in the 68th minute, tucking the ball into the bottom corner after the ball fell into his path, before Bryan Mbeumo made it 5-1 to United with a well-taken lobbed effort.

There was still time for Ipswich to reduce the deficit to three and make it 5-2, however, as Julio Enciso robbed Lisandro Martinez before squaring to substitute Chuba Akpom to prod home from close-range.

Article continues below

That is how it ended in Manchester as the Reds secured their first win of the season and bounced back from last weekend's dismal opening defeat at Hull City.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso opens the door for Enzo Fernandez to join Man City in double transfer update
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso opens the door for Enzo Fernandez to join Man City in double transfer update

Chelsea continued their perfect start to the Premier League season with a win over Brighton - but there could be major changes to the squad ahead of Tuesday's deadline

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has hinted that Enzo Fernandez could leave Chelsea in the next 48 hours (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has shown the exit door to Enzo Fernandez - and admitted Pedro Neto could still leave too.

‌



Argentina midfielder Fernandez is desperate to join Manchester City before Tuesday’s transfer deadline and was left out of Chelsea ’s squad again for their win over Brighton.

‌



City are lining up a £130m British record deal and Alonso admitted he made the decision because it was “best for the team.”

‌



Alonso also left the door open for Neto to go before Tuesday’s deadline as the Portugal winger has been attracting interest with Liverpool, one of the teams linked with him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea expect more arrivals before the window - they have been linked with Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara - and Fernandez appears to be on his way out as long as the money is right and the Blues sign a replacement.

‌



Chelsea boss Alonso said: “We'll see. We want the best for the team and that's why we made the decision against Luton and today and anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.

“We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Neto is also an interesting story for Chelsea because the winger is playing as a wing back and his future looks uncertain - but equally he played well against Brighton and could stay.

‌



View 2 Images Alonso has admitted that Pedro Neto could still leave before the window closes

But asked whether he could guarantee Neto would stay, Alonso said: “No, in football I don't guarantee anything, not anyone. But I was very happy with Pedro. He did really well, he played with a lot of energy.

“He is going to be very important for the team for the whole season because he has different special qualities. He is a threat in one-v-one, he attacks very well in the space, he is strong, he is competitive.

Article continues below

“I am happy that he scored, he was really close to scoring another one. I am very happy with Pedro.”

Sports.title: Sons of police officer killed in horror A66 crash lead out dad's beloved Man Utd vs Ipswich
Sports.content:
Sons of police officer killed in horror A66 crash lead out dad's beloved Man Utd vs Ipswich

Manchester United fan PC Matthew Blades was killed in a horror head-on collision with a vehicle that was speeding down the wrong way of the A66 in Teesside last week

View 3 Images The boys were invited to lead Manchester United out today (Image: Getty Images)

The sons of a police officer killed in a head-on crash on the A66 have led Manchester United out at Old Trafford for their Premier League clash against Ipswich Town.

‌



PC Matthew Blades, described by the club as a "proud Red," was killed alongside colleague PC Tom Clough in a head-on crash with a vehicle travelling the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank, in Teeside, last weekend. Middlesborough FC also paid tribute to the officers and their colleagues at Cleveland Police on Saturday, and United invited Blades' two sons and his wife to their home match against Ipswich.

‌



The children led the United squad as mascots, with the club expressing "great sadness" at the deaths of the two officers in the matchday programme. United said: "Matthew was a proud Red, a devoted family man and a police officer who dedicated his life to helping others.

‌



View 3 Images Matthew Blades was a fan of Manchester United (Image: Facebook)

Sky News presenter forced to cut live broadcast after being 'hassled' on air READ MORE :

"For Matt, some of his happiest times were spent watching United with his boys. His wife Sarah and two children will be at today's game, with his sons leading out the Reds as mascots."

‌



An image of Blades with his two sons at Old Trafford featured in the programme, along with a tribute from an unnamed close friend and colleague. "For Matthew, United was a lifelong love, a passion he shared with his family," the tribute read.

"Since Matt's tragic death there has been an extraordinary outpouring of grief and support. That love has been seen in countless tributes and acts of kindness.

View 3 Images The two boys led Manchester United out today against Ipswich

Article continues below

"Today, we remember a fellow Red. A husband. A father. A son. A brother. A friend. A police officer. A man who gave his life in the service of others. Forever our superhero."

Across the Pennines, match officials at Elland Road for Leeds United's fixture against Brentford wore black armbands as referee Tony Harrington was a friend of PC Blades. There was a minute's applause on Saturday in the memory of the two police officers. Pictures of the two men were displayed on screen.

The occupants of the vehicle headed the wrong way down the A66 were Robert Cahill, 23, Jakob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Cole Robert Worthy, 17. All of them died in the crash.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy

Xabi Alonso is already proving a hit with the Chelsea fans and the Blues made it two wins from win against Brighton as Emi Martinez debuted in goal after his move

View 3 Images Xabi Alonso has kept up his perfect Chelsea start

Chelsea fans are notoriously hard to please. But no wonder Xabi Alonso has won them over already.

‌



This was a brilliant, entertaining and terrific seven-goal contest which had the Stamford Bridge faithful singing the new manager’s name.

‌



Let’s not forget they did not sing Enzo Maresca’s name or Liam Rosenior. And Alonso is a former Liverpool player so it could easily have been a hard sell.

‌



But not with Chelsea playing like this. Yes, they conceded three and look shaky at the back but they are also the great entertainers. Joao Pedro was electric, scored and played comedy villain with an own goal in front of the Brighton fans who gave their former striker pelters all afternoon.

Predictably, Cole Palmer stole the show with the all-important fourth goal to seal victory as he looks rejuvenated after his summer break through missing the World Cup.

Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit READ MORE :

Aston Villa and Chelsea relationship as Emi Martinez becomes EIGHTH transfer READ MORE :

Emiliano Martinez made his debut for Chelsea and, even though they concede far too many goals, at least they have top quality keeper behind their rather unreliable defence.

‌



Pedro Neto shone in his new role as right wing back and Chelsea look as if they could be realistic title challengers this season. Chelsea’s trip to reigning champions Arsenal next Sunday already looks like a blockbuster.

But really it is the flair, the movement and skill of Chelsea’s front three. Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers are as good as any forward line in the Premier League. Certainly no-one missed Enzo Fernandez who was missing again as he waits on a mega last-minute move to Manchester City while the only real concern was Moises Caicedo limping off just 14 minutes after coming on as a substitute.

View 3 Images Chelsea have scored seven goals in their opening two games

‌



But it is the entertainment value which gets Chelsea fans off their seats. They were ahead after just four minutes. Joao Pedro’s header was cleared off the line, but Mats Wieffer got in a horrible mix-up with keeper Bart Verbruggen and Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia pounced to squeeze home.

Incredibly, that was Lavia’s first goal in four very injury disrupted years. His last goal was on August 30, 2022, for Southampton against Chelsea. Maybe this season maybe the year where the talented midfielder’s luck changes.

Chelsea made it 2-0 after just 14 minutes. Jorrel Hato’s throw-in found Morgan Rogers and his low cross was swept in by Pedro Neto. Brighton’s bench were furious because Hato’s throw was so obviously taken from the wrong place.

‌



Joao Pedro missed a sitter to the delight of the Brighton fans. But their glee did not last long. Hato showed great strength to hold off Wieffer and then put over a low cross for Joao Pedro to score. It was 3-0.

View 3 Images Emiliano Martinez made his debut after joining from Aston Villa

Just three minutes later, Brighton gave themselves a glimmer of hope. Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas went through, Chelsea new boy Martinez saved bravely at his feet but Malick Yalcouyé smashed the loose ball in off the far post.

‌



Chelsea have not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since last January. And worse was to follow. Martinez can expect to be busy. Then the comedy punchline. Pascal Gross’s low cross was deflected in off Joao Pedro. The Brighton fans were lapping it up and, from 3-0 down, the fightback was on. This had turned into a sensational game at 3-2.

But Brighton could not seize the opportunity. It was left to Palmer to steal the show again. Palmer strode forward from midfield, had time to pick his spot and fired into the bottom corner to make it safe at 4-2.

Still there was time for one more goal as Gross got a third for Brighton in the 96th minute. Clean sheets are a worry but who cares when you play such great attacking football? Chelsea fans don’t seem bothered.

Sports.title: Donald ends retirement to make dramatic Rams return
Sports.content:
Aaron Donald has officially come out of retirement and will return for the Los Angeles Rams this season.

The 35-year-old is coming back after two and a half years away from the game to form a defensive pairing with Myles Garrett that will alarm every offensive line in the NFL.

The Rams confirmed Donald's decision on Sunday at the end of weeks of talks and almost two months of workouts at the club's facility, where Donald tested whether his body could stand another season. He has signed a one-year contract, with ESPN reporting the deal is worth at least $20m and built heavily on incentives.

Donald walked away without warning in March 2024 after 10 seasons spent entirely with the franchise in St Louis and Los Angeles, a career that brought three Defensive Player of the Year awards, 10 Pro Bowl selections, eight All-Pro honours and a Super Bowl ring, and established him as one of the defining defensive players of his generation.

It was the Rams' trade for Garrett this summer that set the comeback in motion. The former Cleveland Browns star has won two of the last three Defensive Player of the Year awards, meaning the new team-mates own five of the past nine between them.

They join a side already installed as favourites for a second Super Bowl under Sean McVay before Donald's return was even confirmed.

Matthew Stafford, the reigning MVP, leads a Rams offence that ranked first in the league and returns every major contributor, while cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson have arrived from Kansas City to strengthen the other side of the ball.

Donald's 111 career sacks remain a franchise record and the second-most in NFL history by a player operating primarily inside, where his ability to collapse pockets between the tackles drew constant double teams and created space for team-mates throughout his first decade.

Returning resets the clock on a Hall of Fame induction that had been due to become possible in 2029, a price Donald has accepted for the chance to chase a second ring alongside Garrett and a young supporting cast of Byron Young, Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske – starting with the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia next month.

Sports.title: Britain's Samuel causes huge shock as Boulter wins but Norrie bows out at US Open
Sports.content:
Britain's Toby Samuel won his maiden Grand Slam match after an impressive straight-sets victory while Katie Boulter also won through, but Cameron Norrie lost on the opening day of the US Open.

Samuel, who came through three rounds of qualifying, stunned former top 20 player Tomas Machac 6-2 6-3 6-2 in just 90 minutes with a superb display of serving and groundstroke hitting.

The win means Samuel will move into the top 100 on the ATP rankings and he will play 18th seed Jiri Lehecka, another Czech player, in the next round on Wednesday

"I'm so tired - but otherwise I'm so happy to have got the job done there," said Samuel, who was ranked 683 in the world this time last year.

"I played a great match - I'm just so thankful to everyone that has supported me to this moment, and hopefully I can carry on into next week.

"The first two sets I wasn't missing any balls. In the third, he came out a bit stronger - I had a little dip in the first few games, but I came out of it quickly. I'm just going to try and do exactly what I did today in the next match."

Samuel was a clear step above Machac for most of the match with early breaks in the first and second set enough to take a quick two sets lead.

The 23-year-old barely made any unforced errors and was not threatened on serve until the start of the third set, when he was broken, but he won six consecutive games to break his winless Grand Slam duck.

Boulter wins three-set thriller to kick off her campaign in style

Image: Katie Boulter battled her way into the second round at Flushing Meadows

In the women's draw Katie Boulter came through a tough match against American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee.

British number one Boulter, 30, looked to be cruising through at a set and a break ahead, only for some costly double-faults to let Lee back in.

However Boulter, cheered on by new husband Alex De Minaur, gathered herself on a noisy, partisan Court Five to win 6-4 3-6 6-0.

A tricky assignment could await in round two, however, with a potential tie against this year's Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova.

Norrie beaten in first round for third consecutive major

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Norrie crashed out of the US Open in the first round as Luca Van Assche came from a set down to win in four

Norrie was unable to join Samuel in the second round after a third successive first-round exit at Grand Slams this year as he lost 7-6 (8-6) 2-6 2-6 3-6 to France's Luca Van Assche.

A topsy-turvy opening set went Norris' way but his performance suddenly dipped early in the second set and he was never able to recover as Van Assche gained confidence in the long baseline rallies.

Image: Norrie was visibly frustrated with his performance

Norrie, who has been overtaken as British No 1 by Arthur Fery after his run to the Winston-Salem final on Saturday, became increasingly frustrated but showed some fight after being broken early in the fourth set.

He got back to 3-3 with some superb hitting but Van Assche resisted the late rally to break again and book a spot in the second round of the US Open for the first time in his career.

"It was really tough," said Norrie. "I was pretty nervous and it showed in the beginning of the first set, and I did well to steal that first set.

"But I could never really maintain a good level of energy and momentum, and I'd play well for a little bit and then drop off a couple of games here and there.

"So that was super frustrating and pretty surprising. I felt like I lost to myself today."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford’s Manchester United return feels like a marriage of convenience | Will Unwin
Sports.content:
The first chant of the match was for Marcus Rashford, Manchester United’s returning rogue son, the one banished for 18 months, first to the Midlands and then Catalonia. Every football fan loves an academy product who has risen up the ranks, from scrawny child to getting 76,000 off their seats. Rashford is one of these, living out the dream of everyone inside Old Trafford and they are willing to forgive but want something in return.

Not since 7 December 2024 has Rashford been seen in red at Old Trafford. Then it was as a substitute forlornly trying to turn things around in an eventual 3-2 defeat by Nottingham Forest. His relationship with Ruben Amorim was already deteriorating, the second head coach to have become irritated with Rashford. After loans with Aston Villa and Barcelona, everyone is surprised to see him back; it feels like a marriage of convenience because of a lack of offers and securing a replacement was deemed complex.

At Hull, Rashford came on at the break for Patrick Dorgu after a dispiriting 45 minutes but floundered down blind alleys as he tried to spark a listless team into action. The truth is, Michael Carrick needs someone of Rashford’s experience and quality to be at the forefront of this latest attempt of building a successful era. He cannot have any off-field misdemeanours or sulking on the pitch when things are tough.

Carrick is more willing to put an arm around the shoulder, understanding of the pressures that come with playing for United. That is increased when the situation is dire, being behind at home against a promoted club a week after being beaten by another. It is a test of character, one United have failed too often in recent times.

Rashford’s ability has never been doubted: this is someone who did not look out of place at Barcelona and spent the summer playing for his country at the World Cup. In the buildup to the tournament, he went away and worked privately, inviting former teammates to help him to train in Miami, showing a dedication to his craft.

At 28, he should be a leader and Carrick is giving him the opportunity to be one. United have the teenagers Shea Lacey and JJ Gabriel waiting for opportunities, and Rashford is someone they can learn from, having witnessed more than most. He started brightly against Ipswich on the left wing, with United eager to target Dara O’Shea on that side. Rashford can go either way, pushing past a defender to reach the byline or cut in. He tried both, creating dangerous situations with his crossing but without a striker capable of finding the finish.

While Bruno Fernandes, rightly, takes the headlines with his hat‑trick, everyone knows United cannot rely on one man, however influential he may be. Following Fernandes’s example has not always been part of the Rashford playbook but seeing his influence on a team should offer some inspiration for the England international to reach the levels he and United expect. Rashford was certainly not at his best but his head remained high, making runs into dangerous areas, even if the chances of reaching the ball were somewhat forlorn.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes (right) could be an inspiration to Marcus Rashford. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Finishing without a goal or assist when five were scored may irk Rashford but reputations cannot be rebuilt completely in 80 minutes. Willingness needs to be the bare minimum because it will be a long season for United and everyone will need to play their part. On another day, Bryan Mbeumo would not have turned Rashford’s cross on to the bar from a yard out or his saved shot would have beaten the goalkeeper.

Against Hull, barely a clearcut chance was created as United fired blanks, but on Sunday, 33 shots were attempted, 11 of those on target. It was a display of greater intent, energy and productivity, but a long way from flawless as Ipswich were given chances to capitalise on. One reason United were able to cause problems in the second half was down to Rashford and Mbeumo being relentless, occupying defenders and, ultimately, tiring minds and legs with United in the ascendancy.

“Really pleased with Marcus, I am sure it was nice for him to be back and start games and be involved in a good performance,” Carrick said. “I thought he did particularly well in not easy circumstances. I thought he did all round good and will only get better.”

Rashford is United’s No 9 in squad number only, as Carrick is opting to use Benjamin Sesko from the start. When the Slovene is fully fit, a different dimension will be added to the attack, a player used to finishing crosses, which will help Rashford – and others – to thrive. After a year alongside Robert Lewandowski, Rashford is used to having a clinical finisher waiting for service and having an out-and-out striker would benefit him.

Even if few expected Rashford and United to continue their alliance, they are back together. Harmony is not completely restored but both have shown they can make things work,; the affection is evident. The good times and the bad are remembered by both, from the debut goals against Midtjylland to the fallout with Amorim, Rashford’s United story is a rich tapestry, spanning his entire life, and it is not over yet.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta ‘begging’ Premier League to expand 20-man matchday squads
Sports.content:
Arsenal have asked the Premier League to increase the size of matchday squads, with Mikel Arteta saying the current system is detrimental to player welfare. Top‑flight clubs can name 20 players for games, including a minimum of three homegrown players. In Spain’s La Liga, clubs can name a matchday squad of 23, while Italy’s Serie A allows 25.

Arsenal have competed on multiple fronts in recent seasons. Last year, as well as winning the Premier League, they reached the finals of the Champions League and Carabao Cup, as well as the quarter-finals of the FA Cup. With pressure increasing on the football calendar and players facing more matches, Arteta sees no reason why English teams should operate with smaller squads than those from other European leagues.

“I’ve been begging the Premier League if we can extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing, because I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have,” Arteta said, as he prepares for the champions’ trip to Aston Villa on Monday night. “But these are the rules, and within the rules we have to play. We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

Clubs can register a squad of 25 senior players – those aged over 21 – for the season, with at least eight homegrown. As a result, five senior players registered for the season miss out each game. Arteta has said it can be difficult to tell players they are not involved and that the news can negatively affect their wellbeing.

“The question has to be to the players. What do they want? If they raise their hands and say: ‘No, I prefer to stay at home and not travel,’ I think we have an issue because then they don’t love what they do, which is the matchday,” he said. “But I’m sure that if you ask the players, everybody would like to be part of the squad on matchday, because that’s the way that they can fulfil themselves.

“Otherwise you have to tell somebody: ‘You are not even part of this matchday,’ and that’s really tough. And it doesn’t help anybody. It doesn’t help the club. It doesn’t help the valuation of the player. It doesn’t help the player feel part of something. It’s a real issue that has a really simple solution.”

Arteta added: “And all the clubs, because I’ve done the research with all the top clubs in Europe, we are not different to anybody. Most of them, 90% of them, they have more players than us. So we are going to have to deal with that.”

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Ollie Watkins completes move to Al-Hilal from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Al-Hilal have signed Ollie Watkins from Aston Villa, ⁠the two clubs announced on Sunday, as the 30-year-old striker ended a successful ⁠six-year spell with ⁠the ​Midlands club where he became their top scorer in the Premier League. The England international, who had ​two years left on ‌his Villa contract, has moved for a reported £51m.

Watkins ‌signed a three-year contract as Al-Hilal acquired ‌a proven goalscorer after he scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, including five goals in the Europa League as he helped deliver a European trophy to Unai Emery’s side.

However, an ‌exit was on the cards before the transfer window closed, with Emery revealing the ​striker had apologised for making himself unavailable for the club’s Premier League opener, a 4-0 defeat at Brighton.

Watkins scored 91 Premier League goals for Villa and 108 ⁠in all competitions since arriving from Brentford for £28m in ​2020. The striker is among ​a string of departures from Villa ​in the ‌close season following ​the ​exits of key players such as Morgan Rogers and Emi Martinez to Chelsea – the latter moving on Sunday – Ezri Konsa to Arsenal and Youri Tielemans to Manchester United.

Quick Guide How do I 

Roma have stepped up their Serie A challenge with the acquisition of two captains, midfielder Marten De Roon coming over from Atalanta and centre-back Leonardo Balerdi joining from Marseille. The 35-year-old De Roon evolved into Atalanta’s skipper after a decade spent in Bergamo over two spells. He will reunite with Roma’s manager Gian Piero Gasperini, who formerly coached him at Atalanta.

And the former Serie A MVP Rafael Leão has completed a €38m transfer from Milan to Galatasaray. The Turkish side confirmed a deal for the Portugal winger, signing him to a four-year contract with a net salary of €10m per season.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 10: London City Lionesses
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 4th (NB: this is not necessarily Suzanne Wrack’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th

Prospects

Trying to figure out what London City will look like this season, or where they will finish, is nigh on impossible. Eight players have come in as the owner, Michele Kang, bids to continue her drive towards the top of the Women’s Super League and there are some superstars in that group, among them the two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas.

The WSL debutants finished a respectable sixth last season, but were 22 points adrift of the top three. Evidence suggests Kang will be ruthless if the team do not meet her expectations – despite a strong start to the 2025-26 campaign, Jocelyn Prêcheur was sacked as manager shortly before Christmas and replaced by Eder Maestre.

Wholesale changes to teams hoping to break into the top three have proved costly in the past. The hope will be that the level of the players coming in will help London City develop into a side capable of securing Champions League football and challenging for the league. What is clear is that Kang’s spending and ambition is playing a big role in bringing some of the biggest players in the world to the WSL. Mapi León said of her: “Everything counts when you make this kind of a decision, and of course, she was an important part because seeing another woman doing so much to help women’s sports and women’s football grow, I think it’s impossible not to value that. I think it’s something very powerful.”

Off-field picture

London City’s accounts for 2024-25 showed an operating loss of £10.6m and the effect of their big spending before their first season in the WSL, and even bigger spending this summer, will show in future filings. The 2024-25 loss was more than 10 times their £902,000 revenue in that period. Critically, there is a need to grow the fanbase and, with no men’s club supporter pool to draw from, London City will have to be inventive.

The manager

Maestre was appointed in January having previously managed UD Tenerife in Liga F, guiding them to sixth. Maestre’s contract runs until 2028, but he cannot rest on that given Kang’s high expectations. The 42-year-old has shifted the way London City play and a host of new signings could prove fruitful in his system.

Star signing

Mary Earps, León and Kadidiatou Diani have arrived from Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and Lyonnes respectively, but it is the recruitment of Putellas that has rocked the WSL. The 32-year-old spent 14 years at Barcelona, helping them to the top of the women’s game, in the process becoming a talismanic figure. Putellas is far from past her prime and had the pick of clubs worldwide when deciding to leave Spain. Her recruitment was a statement of intent from Kang.

View image in fullscreen The 32-year-old Alexia Putellas has plenty to offer London City Lionesses. Photograph: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

Stat attack

London City made more Opta-defined defensive errors that led to goals and conceded more penalties than any other team in the WSL last season. Elene Lete saved one penalty and the players in front of the 24-year-old goalkeeper need to make her life easier.

Set for a breakthrough

Superstars have come through the door this summer, meaning Nicole Anyomi is one that has slipped under the radar and could go on to make a big impression. Anyomi is a little bit of an unknown to UK audiences having played all her club football in Germany. The forward scored 60 goals in 130 games for Frankfurt in five years. She also has four goals in 34 games for Germany.

What they say

“I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed. I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory” – Putellas

Where are they playing their home games?

Hayes Lane in Bromley is far from an ideal ground for such an ambitious club given the 5,150 capacity. The medium- to long-term goal is to upsize, but space for a ground in and around London is limited. Before any move, however, London City need to increase their fanbase.

Sports.title: Chelsea hold off Brighton in 4-3 win but remain chaotic under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
In the fullness of time Chelsea’s surrender against Brighton in April may be seen as the turning point. The humiliation accelerated Liam ­Rosenior’s demise and forced the Stamford Bridge hierarchy into a ­reckoning leading to the appointment of Xabi Alonso, a shift in ­transfer ­strategy, the birth of the JP Morgan front three and the end of ­Robert Sánchez’s time in goal.

For now, though, the argument that Emiliano Martínez is the final piece in the jigsaw seems a touch ­premature. With seven goals scored and five conceded while winning their first two league games, it is not hard to see where Chelsea need to improve in order to sustain a title challenge. They have to be savvier when ahead, and although the good has so far outweighed the bad Alonso could do with his side not dropping their guard when they have the ­opposition on the ropes.

Alonso’s cool disappeared as ­Chelsea’s focus dipped after they went 3-0 up against an injury‑hit Brighton inside 32 minutes. ­Stamford Bridge was anxious when a João Pedro own‑goal cut the ­advantage to one just after the hour. Alonso was ­shouting at his bench and it was only when Cole Palmer scored with 16 minutes left that calm was restored.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has won his first two league games as Chelsea manager, but neither have been what you would call relaxing. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Not for long, mind you, given that Brighton still managed to grab a consolation through Pascal Gross deep into added time.

It was that kind of game, Martínez conceding three despite playing well on his debut after joining from Aston Villa for £7.5m. “We can hurt teams,” the Argentina goalkeeper said. “At the back, we need to bring the goals down.”

Alonso agreed. Chelsea have been thrilling in transition – they beat Fulham with 37% possession last Monday and had only 26% against Brighton – but they must tighten up when they visit Arsenal next Sunday.

Equally, few sights will be more captivating this season than Palmer combining with João Pedro and ­Morgan Rogers in attack. Palmer looks refreshed after a summer off and Chelsea will be dangerous when games turn into shootouts. They have so many ways to score. The hope is that there will be more stability with Martínez in position.

Alonso did not hesitate to start Martínez, even though the ­Argentinian lacks match ­practice and joined on Friday. “He felt ready,” Alonso said of Martínez, the first 30‑something player to start for ­Chelsea since ­Thiago Silva in May 2024. “We will feel his ­presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence.”

Chelsea, again in a 3-4-2-1 system, are getting serious. Sánchez was not even on the bench against his old side and needs to leave. There was a huge ovation for Martínez before kick‑off and it was followed by the focus switching to Brighton’s No 1 in the fourth minute, a handling error from Bart Verbruggen allowing Roméo Lavia to put Chelsea ahead after Mats Wieffer had cleared a João Pedro header off the line from a corner.

It was a lovely moment for Lavia. It was four years to the day since the Belgian’s last goal, against Chelsea coincidentally enough. His luck with injuries is hopefully turning.

View image in fullscreen Roméo Lavia was on hand to punish Bart Verbruggen’s early handling error and put Chelsea 1-0 up. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Lavia starting his second consecutive league game was important with Chelsea light in midfield. Moisés Caicedo limped off after coming on in the second half, Reece James started on the bench and Enzo ­Fernández was off ­pining for a move to ­Manchester City, so Malo Gusto moved in from right wing-back to partner Lavia.

Chelsea’s selection issues were nothing compared to Brighton’s problems, though. Fabian Hürzeler did not use the absence of Jack Hinshelwood, Yasin Ayari, Georginio Rutter, Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh as an excuse, but it had an impact.
