Chelsea were rampant. Rogers ­continued his fine start after joining from Villa, creating the second goal with a powerful surge away from Luka Vuskovic in the 14th ­minute. Brighton were caught cold by a throw‑in and Rogers crossed for Pedro Neto to score.

Linked with a move away this summer, Neto has been repurposed by Alonso as a wing-back and was bright. João Pedro missed a chance after strong pressing from the ­Portugal international. The away end jeered but João Pedro converted his next opportunity, when a Rogers flick sent Jorrel Hato flying down the left to set the former Brighton striker up.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro rather summed up Chelsea’s start under Xabi Alonso with a goal, an assist and an own goal. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea’s mistake was thinking it was over. Brighton responded before half‑time, Malick Yalcouyé ­volleying in after Martínez made a brave block from ­Charalampos ­Kostoulas. “They showed belief in their quality,” ­Hürzeler said of his players.

The German thought Brighton deserved more. Chelsea were wobbling when João Pedro diverted a Gross cross past Martínez. Diego Gómez then lashed a shot wide and Martínez denied Olivier Boscagli the equaliser.

Alonso needed his big players to step up. Palmer, who had earlier sidefooted over from close range, delivered when he took a João Pedro flick and bent a shot past Verbruggen. Chelsea will be anything but dull.

Sports.title: Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor applies the finishing touch to sink Fulham
Sports.content:
At the final whistle Álvaro Arbeloa provided a study in pensiveness while Régis Le Bris simply looked relieved. For protracted periods an almost palpable fear of losing formed the subtext of a match decided when two of the Sunderland manager’s ­second-half substitutes, Habib Diarra and Wilson Isidor, combined for the latter to score.

Isidor’s goal not merely supplied Sunderland with their first win of the season while leaving Arbeloa’s side pointless, but also ended his side’s 17‑year run without a Premier League home victory against Fulham.

“It wasn’t our day for sure,” said Marco Silva’s successor, whose team were confounded repeatedly by Sunderland’s outstanding central defender Nordi Mukiele.

“We need to improve many things, for sure, especially the energy and the attitude.

“It was a tough game for us. Sunderland were better for many ­minutes. It’s not easy here. If you want to come to Sunderland and play the way you want to, then you need the right mentality. We need to show more energy and fight for every ball.”

Le Bris was a little happier, ­saying: “We didn’t create enough. Fulham were well organised but we had a good balance to manage the transitions. We had to be smart. It’s a question of balancing risk and organisation.”

The tone of a cagey, risk‑averse first half dominated by Fulham’s ­cautious low block was raised, albeit sporadically, by a typically indus­trious central-midfield performance by Sunderland’s Noah Sadiki.

The visiting gameplan seemed all about ouncing on the counterattack but the Democratic Republic of the Congo international extinguished so many potential visiting fires that Fulham’s sole real chance during the opening 45 minutes involved Josh King finding himself confounded by geometry as he miscued a tightly angled opening conjured by Alex Iwobi. Otherwise the home goalkeeper, Robin Roefs, was left pretty much undisturbed.

That apart, a slightly nervous impasse endured. Despite dominating possession, Sunderland’s attacking edge proved anything but serrated, leaving Bernd Leno severely underemployed in Fulham’s goal.

It all left both Le Bris and Arbeloa with much to ponder at the interval. If the watching Sunderland owner, Kyril-Louis Dreyfus, required a reminder as to precisely why Le Bris is so keen to sign a specialist right winger and another striker before the transfer window’s closure he received it.

View image in fullscreen Wilson Isidor salutes the fans after scoring. Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty Images

At least Sunderland’s manager had the excellent Mukiele restored to his backline following injury. The former Paris Saint-Germain defender’s importance on Wearside was, not for the first time, underscored as, early in the second half his tremendous sliding challenge blocked Gonzalo García’s path to a near certain goal following Sander Berge’s stellar through pass.

“I was really impressed with Nordi and I told him this,” Le Bris said. “Nordi showed us today that he’s a great player.”

García, meanwhile, had scored twice in his first two games since joining Fulham from Real Madrid but found Sunderland’s rearguard difficult to decode. Nonetheless, ­perhaps sensing that the visitors were ­gaining a slight initiative, Le Bris made a ­double substitution.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On came Diarra and Isidor for the hitherto largely ineffective Nilson Angulo and Brian Brobbey. Within minutes Sunderland should have been ahead after Enzo Le Fée played a beautiful, first-time ball across goal.

It seemed easier for the on-rushing Isidor to score than miss but, somehow, he ended up striking the base of a post and, in the technical area. Le Bris was left sinking to his knees in disappointment after making a premature celebratory leap as the delivery left Le Fée’s boot. “It was such a good chance,” he said. “It was such a shame.”

Poor Isidor looked mortified but redemption beckoned. Just moments later he surged onto another fabulous low dispatch across the box – from Diarra this time – and atonement arrived as his high-velocity shot whizzed past Leno.

Diarra and Isidor had succeeded in breathing new life into Sunderland’s suddenly much more dynamic press – not to mention capitalising on ­Fulham’s high defensive line – but the former’s cameo was to prove short‑lived after an injury necessitated his replacement by Chris Rigg.

No matter, he and Isidor, had already done just enough. “Habib is so, so intense,” Le Bris said. “He and Wilson changed our press, it was tactically the same just with 20-30% more energy. But the most important thing is, as we saw this afternoon, that the core of this group are very good.

“The players are all in. You can’t play at this level if you’re not all in and well connected with the project of the club. If we can add one or two signings that can help this group then we’ll do it. But I have trust and con­fidence in this squad.”

How Arbeloa must wish he could say the same.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin cancels out Schade’s opener as Leeds salvage point against Brentford
Sports.content:
These nascent moments of the new season can often provide false hope but, as both sets of players shook hands after what was indisputably the correct result at Elland Road, it was difficult not to imagine we had just witnessed a contest between two sides that should have lofty ­ambitions for the months ahead.

Leeds and Brentford were vic­torious on the opening weekend in differing circumstances. Leeds crafted a hard-earned but ultimately deserved win at Nottingham Forest, while Brentford Tottenham. Time will tell what the ceiling of both these sides is but, as they each continued their unbeaten starts here, hopes should be high.

This was a thoroughly ­entertaining game but it was also an occasion in which both managers, as well as the players, displayed their importance to their respective clubs.

Managers are scrutinised at every turn but Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews both excelled here. Both have had question marks as to whether they were the right man to take their team forward: Andrews when he was surprisingly appointed just over a year ago, and Farke in the difficult early stages of last season.

Andrews’s tactical nous was at its peak in the first half. He nullified the Leeds back five and his team led at half-time and probably should have been more than a single goal in front. Kevin Schade’s wonderful flick to turn home a Keane Lewis-Potter cross was the least the visitors deserved.

However, Farke showed his own tactical flexibility at the break. The German was under immense pressure last November and at real risk of losing his job before a move to a back five away at Manchester City proved the catalyst to transform Leeds’s season. He did the reverse here, going back to a four and matching Brentford in the second half to great effect.

Spearheaded by the impact of Ao Tanaka and Lukas Nmecha, both on as substitutes, the hosts were the stronger of the two sides after half‑time. They ultimately got the equaliser their play deserved when ­Nmecha’s shot across goal was prodded home by Dominic Calvert-Lewin to ensure it would be a point apiece, and four from the first two for both sides.

The early evidence overall? Leeds and Brentford should both be ­looking upwards this season. “It’s definitely a good point,” Farke said. “It was a very difficult and complicated game like we expected. Brentford were ­excellent in the first half and deserved to be in the lead, but I’m so proud of our reaction.”

His side struggled to get to grips with Brentford’s shape in the first half. Ethan Ampadu and Anton Stach were overrun in midfield, with the visitors’ three of Vitaly Janelt, ­Mamadou ­Sangaré and ­Mikkel Damsgaard ­running riot. James ­Trafford was called into action on multiple occasions, with smart saves to deny Igor Thiago and Schade.

Such was the strength of Brentford’s momentum that a goal felt inevitable. It duly arrived as half‑time approached when Lewis-Potter’s cross caught the Leeds backline off‑guard and Schade, with his back to goal, turned the ball home expertly to silence Elland Road.

As mentioned, perhaps the ­biggest gripe at that stage was that ­Brentford’s lead wasn’t greater. “I thought we could have done more in the first half,” Andrews said.

“We could have tested Trafford more but we were outstanding. The storm was always going to come and they were forced into ­making changes they haven’t done for quite some time.”

Those changes were pivotal. The back five was abandoned, with Leeds adding Tanaka as an extra man in midfield. It provided an instant impact, with the balance of play shifting the way of the hosts. James Justin forced a clever save from Caoimhín Kelleher before Dan James, on as a substitute, arguably could have done better after being set free on halfway.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In contrast, Brentford were struggling without as much space in the middle, with Igor Thiago cutting a slightly isolated and frustrated ­figure. The Leeds supporters, sensing the momentum was now with them, were beginning to come alive – as were their team. Just like in the first half, a goal was starting to feel more like an inevitability than a possibility.

Farke tweaked things further, with ­Nmecha pro­viding direct support for Calvert‑Lewin, and the duo combined with 11 ­minutes ­remaining. Nmecha dragged a shot across goal to leave Kelleher flat‑footed, with Calvert‑Lewin ­poking into the empty net for his first of the season.

A draw was the least Leeds deserved. Both sides showed their ambition by pushing for a winner, though they cancelled each other out in the final moments to underline further that these are two teams who should think positively about what lies ahead.

Sports.title: European football: Bellingham sparks Real Madrid’s cruise to maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
Real Madrid maintained their perfect start to the season in La Liga with a comfortable 4-0 home ⁠win over promoted Málaga on Sunday, scoring three times inside 30 minutes before adding a late fourth.

Jude Bellingham’s brilliant solo opener, an own ⁠goal by the Málaga goalkeeper, ⁠Alfonso Herrero, and ​a sharp Kylian Mbappé volley in effect settled the contest before half-time, with the substitute Arda Guler wrapping up the victory in added time at ⁠the Bernabéu.

The win lifted Madrid to nine points from three matches, two clear of Atlético Madrid and Alavés. Barcelona, fourth on six points with a ⁠game in hand, host Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute ‌with a superb burst through the middle, collecting a loose ball near the edge of the area, gliding past three defenders and firing low beneath Herrero. They ​doubled their lead seven minutes later after Herrero could only palm out Mbappé’s effort. Bellingham headed the rebound back towards goal and, as Herrero and a teammate collided while trying to clear, the ball ended up in the net.

Mbappé then made it 3-0 in the 30th minute, meeting Trent Alexander-Arnold’s cross ⁠with a fine volley from the centre of the box. The second half drifted until Guler, shortly ​after coming on, started ‌and finished a ​slick move, feeding Vinícius Júnior before tapping in the Brazilian’s return pass to complete the rout.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored for the third straight game as Deportivo La Coruña beat Valencia 3-1. The former Arsenal and Chelsea forward, who joined Deportivo from Marseille in the off-season, scored his side’s second goal as the newly promoted side won for the first time this season.

Napoli suffered a 2-1 defeat at home to Como ⁠in Serie A, with all three goals coming in an entertaining opening half. Assane Diao looked the most threatening player in the opening stages ⁠and the winger was instrumental in the visitors’ 17th-minute opening goal. Diao went past ​Mathías Olivera on the right wing ‌and played a pass ‌across to Martin Baturina whose shot on the turn from close to the penalty ‌spot found the bottom corner of the net.

View image in fullscreen Tasos Douvikas scores Como’s second goal against Napoli. Photograph: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Noa Lang missed an excellent chance to equalise, sending a header over from inside the six-yard box, before Napoli drew level on the half-hour mark. Rasmus Højlund collected a pass on the edge of the area and drilled the ball low into the far corner, but Como were back in front four minutes later when Napoli ​were caught napping at the back.

André-Frank Zambo Anguissa underhit a pass back to Amir Rrahmani in his own box, allowing Baturina to nick the ball away. It fell to Tasos Douvikas and Como’s top scorer last season netted his second goal of this ⁠campaign.

Hakan Calhanoglu’s early strike earned Inter a 1-0 win at Cagliari as they continued a perfect start to their title defence. The Turkey midfielder guided home a first-time strike from the edge of the box after nine minutes to make it two goals in two games and set the tone for a first half dominated by the champions in Sardinia.

Curtis Jones made his Inter debut from the bench in the second half, but Inter’s lack of composure in front of goal almost came back to bite them as Cagliari threatened a shock equaliser with a flurry of late chances.

Paris Brunner netted a goal in each half as Monaco beat visiting ⁠Marseille 2-0 to go top of Ligue 1 as the only team to win their first two games.

Monaco ⁠took the lead in the 13th minute when the Marseille defence was caught ball-watching as Brunner leaped between two defenders ⁠to head home a cross from Aleksandr Golovin. Marseille controlled the ball for long ​spells but struggled to create ‌shots on target, with ‌their efforts often blocked by the home side’s resolute rearguard.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Timothy Weah came close ‌to equalising for the visitors in the 53rd minute with a powerful shot from a tight angle that hit the side netting. It was to prove a costly miss as Brunner latched on to a long ball a minute later, speeding away from the defence before nonchalantly cutting ‌inside and slotting the ball in at the far post to make it 2-0.

Yuito Suzuki scored a hat-trick as Freiburg thumped Werder Bremen 4-1, while Schalke’s first game back in ⁠the Bundesliga ended in a 3-0 defeat at Augsburg as they finished with 10 men.

Sports.title: Alan Pardew: £100m for Sandro Tonali is great business for Newcastle, Lewis Miley is better than him
Sports.content:
Alan Pardew: £100m for Sandro Tonali is great business for Newcastle, Lewis Miley is better than him

Former Newcastle United manager Alan Pardew believes that selling Sandro Tonali and keeping Lewis Miley could be a masterstroke.

The Toon sold Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur in a deal that could cost £100million.



4 Tonali's replacement, Lewis Miley, has started both of Newcastle's opening Premier League games and impressed in both Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, Miley has remained on Tyneside and penned a new deal as well.

The former teammates came up against each other on Saturday as Matthias Jaissle's side visited north London.

The Magpies left with a 2-0 victory as Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa scored for Newcastle.



Miley played the full game alongside new midfield partner Nico Gonzalez and shone, while Tonali was taken off well before the end and jeered by the away fans.

And speaking on The Final Word with Natalie Sawyer, Pardew feels as if Newcastle have come out of the situation very well.



He said: "I want to speak about Miley. They have sold Tonali, and I want you to ask me if I'd rather have Tonali or Miley."

So, Sawyer obliged, with Pardew subsequently responding: "Miley, all day long. He's young, he's quick, and he's got great technique.



"He's got great temperament, and I think he is going to be around for the next ten years, and I think he is going to play for England.

"He was outstanding yesterday for a young player, so Newcastle might have done some really good business.

"That is something they might have known in that camp, I am sure Eddie Howe knows it, that Miley could be better than Tonali. It feels like they've moved Tonali on and are letting the young lad spread his wings."

4 Tonali has started both of Spurs' Premier League games so far that have ended in defeat Credit: AFP



4 Newcastle have four points from their first two games and have impressed under Jaissle Credit: Getty

Starboy

Miley only turned 20 this year, but he is entering his fourth season as a professional footballer for Newcastle.

He has changed a lot since being a very impressive teenager.

The midfielder has significantly bulked up and found a way to use his height to dominate, while after battling with Bruno Guimaraes, Tonali and Joelinton for minutes, he now looks to have a set place in Jaissle's midfield.

Miley is closing in on 100 appearances for Newcastle and Jeff Stelling has tipped him to be Young Player of the Year across the whole division.



And his new manager is a huge fan, saying during pre-season: "I don't want to give him a huge responsibility and pressure, and you should also not give him that from outside.

"He has so much potential. We need to let him grow, develop naturally. He gets the full support.

4 Jaissle has identified Miley as a big player for Newcastle Credit: Getty

"But, I'm really much looking forward to see him, 100 per cent fit and ready because of his qualities. It's, it's a, a true, true talent."



Tonali struggling

It might only be two games in for Tonali, but it hasn't been a great start for him.

Spurs have lost the midfield battles against Brentford and Newcastle so far but Roberto De Zerbi claimed after the defeat to Newcastle that his Italian midfielder isn't fully fit yet, despite taking part since the start of pre-season.

However, De Zerbi backed the former AC Milan man to have a big impact as the season goes on.

He said: "I love Sandro Tonali. So, this day is so sad. We are all of us very disappointed for the result, but I love my players more today than the next win we will make.



"I believe more than the Brentford game of our project, I believe in our players, I think [Omar] Marmoush for the first game played very well.

"It was the first game for Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro, they came late and they are crucial for this team, after the World Cup, after two injuries.

"Sandro Tonali is another crucial player. He is not in the right condition, in the best condition yet, maybe physically."

Next up for Newcastle is Bournemouth at home, live and exclusively on talkSPORT and Spurs go to Nottingham Forest later that day.

Sports.title: Ismaila Sarr desperate for Liverpool move as Crystal Palace forward takes drastic action
Sports.content:
Ismaila Sarr is pushing Crystal Palace to sell him to Liverpool, talkSPORT understands.

The Senegal forward is Liverpool's preferred option to replace Cody Gakpo, who is being targeted by Manchester City.

3 Sarr has scored plenty of goals against Liverpool, now he wants to join them Credit: Getty

The Reds had sounded out Palace over a move for the 28-year-old, albeit without lodging an official bid.

However, it is understood the Eagles indicated they were not willing to entertain a sale.

Sarr deletes all trace of Palace

This comes after Sarr removed all pictures of him representing Palace from his Instagram account on Sunday.

At the time of writing, there is only one post on the player's account, which sees him representing Senegal at the World Cup during the summer.

3 Sarr is determined to make a move away from Selhurst Park Credit: Instagram @ismaila_sarr_18

Sarr, who has three years left on his Palace contract, has already been the subject of interest from elsewhere this summer, with Palace rejecting a bid from Turkish giants Galatasaray.

The 28-year-old has not been involved in either of Palace's Premier League matches this season.

What has Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage said about Ismaila Sarr's future?

Palace boss Pierre Sage said Sarr would be available for the opening weekend defeat at Everton.

However, Sage later revealed Sarr had been ruled out due to a groin issue and reiterated he hoped to keep the winger at the club.

When asked if he expected Sarr to stay at the club ahead of Palace's 4-1 defeat to Manchester City on Friday night, Sarr said: "For the moment, yes, because when you have three years on the contract, it is not easy to leave.

"I understand that for everybody to have this kind of contact [from Liverpool] is difficult, because you hesitate a lot. But for the moment, he is with us. He is under contract.

3 Liverpool are scrambling around for wingers with transfer deadline day on Tuesday Credit: Getty

"He is injured and maybe you can make a link between his injury and the situation. But for me, he is honest and I have no problem with that. We just want him on the pitch as quickly as possible."

Sarr has spent the last two seasons with Palace having joined in the summer of 2024 from Marseille.

He has gone on to score 33 goals and contribute ten assists for the Eagles across 92 appearances across all competitions.

In that period, Sarr has helped the club win the FA Cup and the Conference League.

What is the latest on Liverpool's pursuit of a winger?

Liverpool's approach for Sarr comes after their failed pursuit of Yankuba Minteh, with Brighton setting an £80million asking price.

The Seagulls had already knocked back two bids from Liverpool for Minteh, with the latest being £60m.

Liverpool are not expected to return for a third bid unless Brighton's valuation drops.

Liverpool's interest in Sarr comes as they remain active in the market for wide attackers.

Paris Saint Germain's Bradley Barcola is closing in on a move to Anfield, however with the two clubs finally agreeing a fee after protracted talks across the summer.

Sports.title: Water pours on soaked Manchester United fans as Old Trafford roof leaks again after torrential downpour
Sports.content:
Water pours on soaked Manchester United fans as Old Trafford roof leaks again after torrential downpour

The leaky Old Trafford roof reared its ugly head again during Manchester United's 5-2 win over Ipswich Town in the Premier League.

With the Red Devils cruising towards victory in the second half, the heavens opened, and many Man United fans were drenched as the roof failed to deal with the rain.



3 It was a proper August thunderstorm that caused the issues Credit: Getty

The match kicked off under grey skies, but the rain stayed off until deep into the second half.

The heavens then opened and the roof that has caused fans so many problems in the past simply couldn't handle it.

Videos emerged on social media showing the extent of the downpour and just how wet some Manchester United fans were.



But they would have left in good spirits thanks to a comeback win for Michael Carrick's men.

Man United have spent £200million in the transfer market this summer, but the roof still leaks.



This has been a problem for a few years now, with reports stretching back to 2024 about the leaky roof.

At the time, The Guardian revealed that the club knew the roof is prone to leaking but decided against fixing it.



And the problem returned on Sunday afternoon as Man United put the opening weekend defeat to Hull City behind them to win 5-2.

Several Man United fans online, though, couldn't believe how bad the situation with roof was.

One said: “Old Trafford’s roof is still leaking in 2026. New managers. New signings. Same waterfall.”

Another added: “Man United just spent £150m this summer but the Old Trafford roof is still leaking.”



3 Man United defied the poor weather to seal a first three points of the season Credit: AFP

Off and running

After losing to Hull, Man United needed to respond, and they made an awful start.

Luke Shaw was beaten by Abdul Fatawu down the right, and he crossed for Leif Davis.

The left-back guided a half-volley in off the crossbar to give the visitors the lead and leave talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook furious at Shaw.



An unfortunate slip brought Carrick's men back into the game as Matheus Cunha threaded a pass through for Bruno Fernandes, and he rifled home at the near post.

Man United grabbed the lead in the second half as Harry Maguire handled a loose ball and drove in a shot.

3 Maguire benefitted from a loophole in the laws Credit: Getty

The shot was going miles wide and hit Jacob Greaves and went in. As a result, the goal stood because Maguire's effort wasn't on target.



Fernandes got his second from the penalty spot when Greaves scythed Cunha down.

And he soon had a hat-trick when a Bryan Mbeumo effort deflected into his path, and he found the bottom corner.

But that wasn't the end of the scoring as Mbeumo chipped home before Julio Enciso robbed Lisandro Martinez and put the ball on a plate for Chuba Akpom to tap home.

It meant that while a lot of Man United fans left soaking wet, they at least had three points to celebrate.

Sports.title: ‘Part of the problem’ – Manchester United told they must replace ‘awful for years’ player
Sports.content:
‘Part of the problem’ – Manchester United told they must replace ‘awful for years’ player

talkSPORT's Alex Crook was furious with Luke Shaw after Ipswich Town's opener against Manchester United at Old Trafford.

Although the Red Devils won Sunday's game comfortably, they had a scare when Leif Davis put Ipswich ahead after Abdul Fatawu picked up the ball on the right, drove past Shaw as if he wasn't there and picked out Davis.

3 Davis slotted Ipswich into a surprise lead at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

The left-back was unmarked at the far post after getting away from Diogo Dalot, and he guided a left-footed half volley in off the crossbar.

Man United equalised before half time through Bruno Fernandes as Matheus Cunha took advantage of a slip and played the captain in, who slammed home at the near post.

Harry Maguire then rifled in a shot that was going miles wide as the ball hit Jacob Greaves and flew in.

The ball hit Maguire's hands in the build-up, but because his shot wasn't on target, the goal was allowed to stand.

And Greaves rounded off a nightmare few minutes as he went through the back of Cunha and gave a away a penalty that Fernandes stuck away.

And Fernandes grabbed his hat-trick when Bryan Mbeumo's deflected strike dropped kindly to him in the box, and he tucked home. Mbeumo made it 5-1 with a lob late on with Chuba Akpom scoring a stoppage-time consolation goal for the visitors.

However, Crook couldn't hide his rage on GameDay Live when discussing the first Ipswich goal.

It started with talkSPORT's Manchester Correspondent Micky Gray, who said: "What have Manchester United's full-backs been doing in pre-season because they look like they've had it off?

"Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw, I mean, how easy is it far Fatawu to get past Luke Shaw and pick out his man inside the 18-yard-box

"Leif Davis has got himself into an area, where he just has to place that ball first time.

3 Shaw struggled to deal with Fatawu

"It's a difficult finish, but it is a super finish. They've bided their time and waited for their opportunity, but what a super goal."

In response, Crook said: "I've got no words. I've got no words. Luke Shaw was awful at Hull last week. He was awful again there.

"He has been awful for how many years? He is part of the problem. He is part of the reason that Man United don't keep clean sheets.

"He is part of the reason they keep losing football matches and yet, there is no sign of anyone coming in to replace him."

Manchester United 5-2 Ipswich Town

Man United opened their 2026/27 Premier League season with a lot of fanfare and expectation.

They went to East Yorkshire to take on newly promoted Hull City and suffered a shock 2-0 defeat.

3 Fernandes has started the season with a bang and the match ball Credit: Getty

But despite conceding first, they've bounced back in fine fashion Fernandes netted a hat-trick to ease a few concerns around Michael Carrick's side even if a left-back is still a priority.

Man United's need for a left-back

Manchester United have been looking at a left-back all summer, but with time running out in the transfer window, it remains to be seen if they do bring in a left-back.

Newcastle United's Lewis Hall has been heavily linked. However, Matthias Jaissle shut down any suggestion of Hall leaving St James' Park this summer last weekend.

Another option was Myles Lewis-Skelly with the player was offered to the Red Devils, although that was later denied.

Sports.title: Why Manchester United goal stood despite Harry Maguire handball as Premier League explain rule
Sports.content:
Why Manchester United goal stood despite Harry Maguire handball as Premier League explain rule

The Premier League have explained why Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was given despite an apparent handball.

Harry Maguire seemingly handled the ball moments before his shot went in off Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves in United's 5-2 win.



2 Maguire's shot went in off Greaves for an own goal Credit: Getty

It put United 2-1 up after 56 minutes, with replays then showing what appeared to be a handball in the build-up.

VAR checked the incident and kept showing replays of the own goal rather than the handball.

Referee Craig Pawson then pointed to the centre circle to confirm that the goal stood.



Why did the Man United goal stand?

It was an unusual circumstance, but the Premier League Match Centre has explained why it was not chalked off.

"The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball," Professional Referee Organisation, or Pro Ref explain.



VAR Jarred Gillett said: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

The Premier League then published the rules from International Football Association Board (IFAB) on what is deemed to be handball.



United come from behind to beat Ipswich

Sunday's handball drama is likely to spark further debate over the rules, but United and Ipswich still entertained in the seven-goal clash.

Leif Davis put the visitors ahead with just under half an hour played as he smashed into the roof of the net from Abdul Fatawu's cross.

After Marcelino Nunez slipped, Matheus Cunha fed the ball to Bruno Fernandes and the United captain fired in their equaliser.

2 Greaves was the unlucky Ipswich man who found the back of his own net Credit: AFP



United went ahead via the own goal from Greaves, who then gave away a penalty for his foul on Cunha.

Fernandes made no mistake from the spot and completed his hat-trick midway through the second half with a calm finish.

With torrential rain falling from the Manchester sky, Bryan Mbeumo added a fifth goal as his lob crept over the line.

Chuba Akpom netted a consolation goal for Ipswich in stoppage time.

United have picked up their first points and win of the new Premier League season in a much-improved performance from the 2-0 loss at Hull City last weekend.



They sit tenth in the table, with Ipswich two spots below them.

Sports.title: Liverpool star tells club it must keep Cody Gakpo despite Dutch star wanting Manchester City move
Sports.content:
Liverpool star tells club it must keep Cody Gakpo despite Dutch star wanting Manchester City move

Virgil van Dijk has urged Liverpool to keep Cody Gakpo at the club despite the winger wanting a move to Manchester City.

City have submitted an opening offer for Gakpo, but the Reds are reluctant to sell him unless they recruit a replacement.



5 Van Dijk would prefer to see Gakpo remain Credit: AFP

Tottenham Hotspur were also interested in the versatile forward, but he has chosen the Etihad.

Should Gakpo depart, Liverpool may not miss him too much as they have a deal in place for Bradley Barcola to join from Paris Saint-Germain, although the club would ideally like another wide attacker even if the Dutchman departs.

The 27-year-old has enjoyed a good start to the Premier League campaign as well.



He scored in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle United before setting up Alexander Isak in the other 2-2 draw versus Nottingham Forest.

And speaking about Gakpo, Van Dijk was asked if he'd like Gakpo to stay.



"What do you think," Van Dijk responded.

"He's a quality player. I think we should keep quality players.

"Let's see what the next few days bring.

"I want him to stay not only because he's a quality player but also because he's a friend of mine. He's very important for us."

Gakpo's future

Liverpool have officially not been open to selling Gakpo all summer.

5 Gakpo is playing a big part in Liverpool's season so far Credit: Getty



However, with Barcola on the way and a potential other winger as well, that stance is likely to change.

Spurs had thought they could sign the forward, but he has chosen City.

Enzo Maresca's side have put in an offer for Gakpo, with Liverpool hoping to secure around £85million.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs provided the latest on Gakpo.

He said: “Manchester City in the last few days have gone really big on Cody Gakpo. It's taken the player a little bit by surprise because for much of the summer, it was Tottenham and Cody Gakpo. He’d spoken to Roberto De Zerbi.



“But our information is that Cody Gakpo favours Manchester City.

5 Maresca is looking to add some extra firepower Credit: Getty

“As a consequence, this is expected to develop. I actually think that Tottenham now realise they can't do that deal. Do they turn to Iliman Ndiaye as a result?

“Bradley Barcola comes in, as we exclusively revealed this morning, for £106m with £17m in add-ons.

“It may come down to the player realising even if they don't add now another attacker, Victor Munoz has come in and Rio Ngumoha needs a pathway.



"Gakpo maybe in previous seasons could have looked out wide, looked in the centre. But now up front, it's Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitike. Behind them, it's Florian Wirtz.

“So I think he seems to believe that even if it's not now, it might be the beginning of the end.

“This was kind of what Luis Diaz thought when Liverpool wanted to keep the player, but eventually they sold him to Bayern Munich.

5 Iraola has already used Gakpo to great effect to start the season Credit: Getty



“Cody Gakpo has got a big decision to make. From Liverpool's perspective, if they were to sell, they know they're bringing in more money.

“It might mean that they can overpay for an Ismaïla Sarr or a Yankuba Minteh. Then two attackers will come in as well.”

Barcola incoming

Liverpool are set to pay an initial £106million, which could rise to £123m with add-ons for Barcola.

The French international has wanted the move to Anfield all summer, and before the close of the transfer window, he will sign for the Reds.



And Van Dijk is already rubbing his hands at the prospect of having Barcola as a teammate rather than a rival.

"He's a good player, someone with pace, I remember a goal he scored against Chelsea [in the Champions League last season]," Van Dijk said.

5 Barcola appears destined to join the Reds before the window shuts Credit: Getty

"If he comes here then he will be welcomed with open arms.

"I don't think there's any doubt that a club like Liverpool is very attractive to very good players. This is one of the biggest clubs in the world.



"We all know that we're going through a little bit of a transition. You either want to be a part of it or you don't.

"Adding quality to the squad always makes a difference. Let's see what the next few days bring. After Tuesday, we have to fight for everything with no regrets."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso provides update as Moises Caicedo taken off with injury shortly after coming on
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso provides update as Moises Caicedo taken off with injury shortly after coming on

Moises Caicedo was forced off injured just 10 minutes after coming on for Chelsea in their 4-3 win over Brighton.

The midfielder was making his first appearance of the season against his former club, having helped Ecuador to the last 16 of the World Cup, where he captained his country against Mexico.

2 Caicedo's Blues return did not go to plan Credit: Getty

Caicedo's short-lived return to action

Caicedo replaced Pedro Neto on 68 minutes at Stamford Bridge.

But the 24-year-old was quickly having to be substituted himself, going down with summer signing Valentin Barco coming on in his place.

Caicedo was visibly emotional as he made his way back towards the tunnel.

Signed from Brighton for £100m in 2023, he's featured in almost all of the Blues' Premier League games since.

But manager Xabi Alonso played down fears of a lengthy absence for Caicedo, explaining in his post-match press conference that his withdrawal was precautionary.

"It wasn't more than last time," he said. "He was cautious. His feeling was not the best. It wasn't something new."

Alonso's Chelsea scoring and conceding in almost equal measure

His elite defensive midfield acumen could be invaluable for a team so far shipping goals under their new boss, despite starting the campaign with successive victories.

Chelsea began the season with a 3-2 triumph away to west London rivals Fulham.

Alonso and co. take their 100% start into another London derby next Sunday when they travel to champions Arsenal.

As well as their two league victories, the Blues beat League One Luton 2-0 in the Carabao Cup on Thursday.

Caicedo missed the trip to Fulham and visit of Luton through injury but returned to the matchday squad on Sunday.

Chelsea raced into a 3-0 lead inside 32 minutes through two other former Brighton men, Romeo Lavia – scoring his first goal for the Blues – and Joao Pedro, who struck either side of Pedro Neto.

2 Lavia opened the scoring after just four minutes Credit: Getty

The Seagulls fought back through Malick Junior Yalcouye and a Joao Pedro own goal, only for Cole Palmer to put the hosts 4-2 up.

Pascal Gross' late header might have given Fabian Hurzeler's side the slightest sliver of hope, but it was virtually the last action of the game.

Next up for Brighton is a home clash with Leeds on Saturday.

Chelsea stop Brighton rot

It's the first time Chelsea have beaten the Seagulls for almost two years, after a run of three straight defeats in all competitions.

In doing so, they've also won their first two Premier League games for the first time since 2021.

Sports.title: Steve Bruce claims Premier League’s most underrated player doesn’t get praise he deserves
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire is the most underrated player in the Premier League - he's never let Manchester United or England down.

That is the verdict of Red Devils hero Steve Bruce, who believes his former Hull City player doesn't get the accolades he deserves.

3 Bruce named Maguire as his pick for the Premier League's most underrated player Credit: Getty

Maguire, who named himself one of the best defenders in the world in both boxes earlier this year, has long divided opinions among fans.

He joined Man United from Leicester City for £80million in 2019 - a world record transfer fee for a defender, but has had mixed success.

Maguire's ups and downs at Man United

The centre-back has made over 260 appearances for the club and won the Carabao Cup and FA Cup since his arrival.

He was appointed captain just five months after his arrival, but a downturn in form led to criticism of his continued selection under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and his successor Ralf Rangnick.

In 2022, Police even investigated a bomb threat at Maguire's home following a petition to remove him as Man United skipper.

He was stripped of the Red Devils captaincy a year later after he fell out of favour under Erik ten Hag.

Maguire then looked to be heading out the exit door to West Ham, but stayed at Old Trafford and has featured nearly 100 times since, under four different managers, despite the club spending £100m on players in his position in that time period.

The 66-cap England international has also enjoyed a career revival since Michael Carrick took the reins from Ruben Amorim.

His form was rewarded with an international recall in March and a new United contract, but he was controversially left out of the Three Lions' World Cup squad by Thomas Tuchel this summer.

3 Maguire is a key figure under Carrick but was unable to prevent the club's 2-0 defeat to Hull City Credit: Getty

Maguire 'should get more accolades'

Former Man United captain Bruce knows all about being snubbed by his country, having never earned a senior cap during his playing days.

Asked for his pick as the most underrated right now, Bruce told talkSPORT.com on behalf of Free Bets: "Wow, that's a good question.

"In my era, I always thought it was Dennis Irwin. Dennis Irwin played nearly 13 years for Man United. Is there somebody out there like that?

"I always think that Harry Maguire always gets a bad deal, and he always comes around and proves people wrong in my opinion.

"So maybe I'll go for Harry. I don't think he gets the accolades that he should have got, certainly after watching them for the last eight to ten years."

3 England's Mr Dependable, Maguire, missing out was one of the major surprises of Tuchel's World Cup squad Credit: PA

Harry Maguire stats

Maguire can point to the stats that show United's Premier League win rate is better with him in the team than without.

He was a key part of the team who finished third and second in successive seasons under Solskjaer, with an ankle ligament injury ruling him out of the Europa League final defeat to Villarreal.

Since his 2019 transfer, Maguire ranks in the top 10 in his position across the league for progressive carries, aerial duels won, interceptions, and appearances - despite his various fitness issues.

Maguire was also named by UEFA in their Team of the Tournament during the Three Lions' run to the final on home soil in 2021 - and even scored a penalty in the shootout defeat to Italy.

Bruce added to talkSPORT: "I've never seen him let Man United down.

"I've never seen him let England down either, but unfortunately, it seems to hang around him for a long time.

"So he should get more accolades than he does."

Sports.title: US Open star melts down with trainer who REFUSES to treat 'cramp' during medical timeout
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

French tennis star Terence Atmane was embroiled in a furious spat with US Open medical staff after he was refused treatment under the sport's strict rules around cramps.

Players are unable to take medical timeouts during matches if they suffer cramps and can only seek treatment briefly during changeovers or set breaks.

But Atmane was keen to stress that he was suffering from muscular pain separate from cramping - despite having struggled with the issue earlier in his five-set battle against Jaume Munar.

Calling for the physio deep in the fifth set, Atmane became incensed that he was being misunderstood by the responding physiotherapist as they questioned why he needed a medical timeout.

'I need treatment here, this is not cramping,' the 24-year-old said. 'This is pain. I have pain.

'I'm telling you, I have pain. On both sides, before I was cramping, and now I have pain. You don't understand? No, you don't understand. I need treatment, I really need treatment right now.'

Terence Atmane boiled over after he was refused a medical timeout after being deemed to have suffered cramp by the physio

The Frenchman had previously been treated in a break in play but continued to struggle with 'pain' in the fifth set

When told that he could not be treated if he was suffering cramp, Atmane turned up the volume.

'This was not cramp, it's pain. It was pain,' he raged. 'Excuse me, can you please give me treatment, and stop acting stupid. Is it possible to have some common sense? I tell him I have pain, why is he telling me no? I have pain.'

The tournament supervisor, called onto court to attend to the issue, urged Atmane to remember that the physio was a 'medical professional'.

'It's my body. I have pain on both there, so I need treatment there,' Atmane replied, before speaking over the physio.

'What do you mean come on man? I'm telling you I have pain on both my legs. P-A-I-N,' Atmane spelled out. 'Pain. Not cramp. I know the rules, that's why I'm asking you. It's not a cramp, it's pain.'

Despite his protestations, Atmane was refused treatment, but was unable to take no for an answer as the physio walked away.

'Come back, come back,' he called. 'What's your credentials? I don't know your name. No, no no, come back.'

Atmane then rounded on the umpire as he was ordered to return to play, adding: 'I have pain, and the guy says no. I'm telling him I have pain, and the guy says no. What does it matter? I get the name after this.'

During the third set, Atmane became so badly impaired with a muscular issue that he was almost unable to move

The 24-year-old was only able to serve underarm and lost the set 6-1 after building a strong two-set lead

Earlier in the match, Atmane was suffering so severely he was forced into limited movement and underarm serving in the third set.

The Frenchman was two sets up against the Spaniard when he began to struggle, and first received medical timeout for a leg issue, before continuing to play impaired.

Munar disagreed with the decision to award Atmane a timeout, and later accused Atmane of time-wasting and receiving extra on-court coaching, calling for the supervisor to complain directly.

Atmane went on to receive a time violation for repeatedly taking too much time between points.

World No. 55 Munar complained about his opponent's conduct again in the fifth set after Atmane's rant, but the pair exchanged a civil - if curt - handshake after Munar beat his rival 6-7(5), 3-6, 6-1, 7-6(4), 7-5.

Speaking to Daily Mail Sport after the match, Atmane said: 'It's very simple. I told (the physio) I had pain on my leg after the cramp, and then he told me that that was not true, and it was cramp.

'So I told him that what he was saying was not true because I had pain, and then he didn't want to treat me. So then after he left, simple as that. There's nothing I can do about it.

'I told him it was pain and not cramp because I was cramping before and it was like different kind of pain, and he didn't want it to treat me. So I said to him like, I mean, there's no point to fight. So that's it.

The drama on Court 13 throws into perspective the cloudiness which surrounds the rule, with the guidelines often criticised for inconsistent enforcement.

Cramps are classified as a fitness issue, rather than injury or illness, with many players turning to esoteric methods like drinking pickle juice on-court to stave off the dehydration often at the root of the problem.

But at this year's Australian Open, a tussle between Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev over the former's on-court treatment turned ugly with the German accusing the tournament of not adhering to the regulations.

The Career Grand Slam winner had been badly affected by the challenging heat in Melbourne, throwing up multiple times during their semi-final.

His movement was later affected, and Alcaraz went on to request a medical timeout, which was granted.

'He has cramps,' Zverev told the supervisor as Alcaraz received treatment. 'What else should it be? This is absolute bulls***.'

'That is unbelievable. That can not be. You can not be serious,' he continued in a mixture of German and English.

But Atmane said that he did not advocate for a change in the regulations, despite his experience on Sunday.

'I think that's fair that we cannot receive treatment when we have cramps,' Atmane added. 'I feel like it has always been like this, so I don't see why it should change.

'Even if today I was fully cramping, I never asked for the physio at that time. I feel like rules are rules, and we should respect them. It was a little bit unfortunate that he didn't wanted to treat the problem that I had, but it is what it is. At the end of the day, I lost, and it happened.'

Sports.title: Gary Neville accuses Liverpool of 'leaving Andoni Iraola short' with 'bizarre' recruitment: Pundit sends warning to Reds boss as he hits out at failure to sign full-backs and criticises decision to sell Cody Gakpo
Sports.content:
Gary Neville has accused Liverpool of leaving Andoni Iraola with an uncompetitive squad due to their 'bizarre' transfer dealings this summer.

The pundit is flabbergasted to see the Reds potentially selling Cody Gakpo to rivals Manchester City for £85million.

And he cannot believe they have failed to sign a full back and a holding midfielder - a shortcoming which will see them 'concede a lot,' according to Neville.

Liverpool have had to settle for two 2-2 draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest to start the season and look vulnerable whenever the opposition attack.

Neville said on his podcast: 'It's bizarre. The noise that Gakpo might leave - I know that Barcola might come in - but he looks like their best forward. I think he's a real danger.

'Someone like him can maybe not be appreciated at times. He's always involved and you should never underestimate a player [like him]. There's a lot of scruffy things he does but he always keeps coming back, he always wants the ball and he's always there. He does contribute with goals and with assists, maybe not at a massive level, but it's hard to replace lads like him.

Gary Neville has accused Liverpool of 'leaving Andoni Iraola short' despite their summer spend

He does not trust the defensive credentials of Milos Kerkez (above) and Jeremie Frimpong

'When your main opponents are looking to take him off you, I always think that is a bit of a worry and I don't think they can afford to lose him.

'But what's the most bizarre is that they haven't signed a full-back, left back and a right back. [Milos] Kerkez and [Jeremie] Frimpong look like the ideal wing-backs in a back five. It looks like a squad that could play a back three.

'If they're going to play a back four, and Kerkez and Frimpong are going to play full-back, and they're not going to sign a holding midfielder, Liverpool are going to concede a lot of goals.

'With the two goals against Forest, the right back is nowhere to be seen on the first one and on the second one, he lets the runner go from a throw-in when he should just mark him and go with him all the way. He's not got a natural instinct of how to defend.

'We used to criticise Trent Alexander-Arnold for his defensive work. To put this into context, TAA is a lot better defender than Frimpong, and he used to contribute 15-20 assists in a season. I don't think Frimpong will.

'Kerkez doesn't look like he's settled. At one point last season I thought he looked like an academy player playing at left-back for Liverpool and he's not - he's a very good player but they can't play with those two at full back and expect not to concede goals.

'I'm not sure what's going on there in respect of their recruitment. I don't think they have the numbers in defence. I think they're leaving Andoni Iraola well short. I know he looks like a gentleman and you see him in the interviews but if I was him I'd be demanding something in the next 48 hours because it will cost him.

'They will concede a lot of goals if those two play at full back in a normal traditional back four with that midfield.

He cannot comprehend the prospect of them selling Cody Gakpo to Manchester City for £85m

Neville says that Iraola should be 'demanding' more signings from Liverpool's hierarchy

'There's real excitement with the players they've got up top and if they added a defensive midfield player, and two good full backs, they'd have a really good chance.

'But they're being undermined by a lack of recruitment in those full back areas and in central midfield. They need to do something.'

Liverpool have at least addressed their shortage at centre-back, bringing in Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes for £60m and Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona.

Up top, Bradley Barcola is poised to sign from Paris Saint-Germain for £123m, and they have already added Victor Munoz, who scored his first goal against Forest, for £34m from Osasuna.

But the Reds have never truly replaced Fabinho in the No 6 role.

They do have Conor Bradley and Kostas Tsimikas as back-ups in the full-back areas, but they are not known for being overly defensive either.
