Sports.title: Why Michael Carrick should be concerned despite Man United's thrilling comeback win over Ipswich as Bruno Fernandes comes to the rescue again, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
By the time the heavens opened over Old Trafford, the lightning flashed, the thunder rumbled overhead and the roof sprang another leak, the proverbial storm clouds gathering over Manchester United had long since passed.

But for ten minutes before half-time, United were facing the unthinkable scenario of losing their opening two games of the season to newly-promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town.

The visitors from East Anglia led through a Leif Davis goal and were threatening to plunge Michael Carrick and his team into crisis before August is out and the transfer window has closed by winning here for the first time since 1984.

United deserve credit for responding to adversity so emphatically in a quite barnstorming game of football. They got a couple of lucky breaks, not least when Marcelino Nunez’s slip led to the equaliser and the second goal was allowed to stand after Harry Maguire wasn’t penalised for handball. Who thinks up these rules?

Having been given a nudge in the right direction, United took full advantage with a second-half onslaught that was as relentless as the deluge that battered this old place. Carrick wants his team to play on the front foot, and a total of 33 shots – their most in a decade – suggests he is on the right track, whatever concerns exist over his defence.

Once again, United were mightily grateful to their inspirational captain Bruno Fernandes for dragging them out of the mire. Fernandes scored a hat-trick – the third of his Old Trafford career – and got a first assist of the season after making a Premier League record 21 of them last term.

Not for the first time, it was captain Bruno Fernandes who rescued his team with a standout performance that ended with him claiming a hat-trick and another assist

Harry Maguire was allowed to get away with a handball in the build-up to the second goal

The scoreline certainly felt a little harsh on Ipswich given how they competed in the first half, but Gary O'Neil's men were simply swept away after half-time

At the end of a week in which he received the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award in recognition of his feat, Fernandes provided yet more evidence of his enduring importance to this team.

There hasn’t been quite the same level of speculation over his future as a year ago, but with ten months left on a contract that includes an option for United to extend it by another year until June 2028, it still feels as though he is the one player that United simply can’t do without.

On the day Carlos Baleba was paraded on the pitch before kick-off, and other midfield signings Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos made their home debuts, here was Fernandes stealing the show again.

There were other big plusses for Carrick. Kobbie Mainoo was selected ahead of Santos and showed how important he will be if the £155million midfield rebuild is to be a success.

Marcus Rashford made his first United start for 626 days and showed the raw enthusiasm that turned him into a local hero before it all went wrong and he drifted away to Aston Villa and Barcelona on loan. We wondered how Old Trafford would react to his return, but there was genuine warmth from the stands.

There are still cracks that this win won’t paper over, in particular the issue at left-back which has lingered all summer and shows no signs of going away with two days to go until the window closes.

Luke Shaw was exposed at Hull and it took Ipswich less than half an hour to do the same. Shaw was left for dead by Abdul Fatawu who got away down the right and crossed to Davis who had been left unmarked by Bryan Mbeumo and met it with a first-time effort.

Senne Lammens had already bailed United out with vital saves from Julio Enciso and Daizen Maeda, but he couldn’t prevent the ball going in off the underside of the bar.

Shaw looked vulnerable in the defeat at Hull, and he was left for dead in the build up to the Tractor Boys' opener

New £70million signing Carlos Baleba was paraded on the pitch before kick-off but might not make his debut until mid-October due to an ankle injury

Having failed to sign a left-back so far, surely United have to do so before Tuesday's deadline.

They were presented with a rather fortunate opportunity to level the scores in the 40th minute when Nunez slipped as he controlled a pass close to halfway, and Matheus Cunha guided an excellent early pass beyond Sasa Lukic and into the path of Fernandes.

Did United’s captain have the legs to get away from his opponent? Probably not so he took one touch and then lashed the ball past Kjell Scherpen.

After Mbeumo somehow hit the bar from point-blank range early in the second half, United transformed the game with two goals in the space of five minutes.

The first felt very harsh on Ipswich after Maguire challenged Chuba Akpom just outside the penalty area and clearly used his hands to control the ball. The United defender advanced into the box and fired a low shot which was going wide until it hit Jacob Greaves, which not only diverted the ball past Scherpen but also negated the handball because it was an own-goal.

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil accepted the ‘strange rule’ with good grace, but summed up the sense of injustice around it. ‘Sometimes you see a goal and think it shouldn’t stand, and that felt like one of them,’ said O’Neil, who also had the misfortune of losing record signing Emersonn to a knee injury at half-time.

It got worse for Greaves when he tripped Cunha as he raced onto Mainoo’s excellent throughball and Fernandes scored from the spot.

Then after Mainoo and Mbeumo both had efforts blocked, the ball ran kindly for the Portugal star to slot home for his hat-trick.

As the storm raged overhead, Fernandes sent Mbeumo through to lob Scherpen for the fifth, before Enciso picked Lisandro Martinez’s pocket and squared for Akpom to score.

It mattered not but was another reminder that United still have work to do despite the scoreline.

Sports.title: Roger Federer can't stop crying after wife's emotional speech as tennis legend inducted into Hall of Fame
Sports.content:
Roger Federer was moved to tears as he was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame after an emotional introduction from his wife Mirka.

The Swiss superstar became eligible for the honour this year, five years after his competitive retirement, with his 20 men’s Grand Slam titles unmatched by all but his greatest rivals Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic.

During his playing career, the 45-year-old often struck an emotional figure on the court, but as he was formally written into the annals of tennis history in Rhode Island, Federer was at times unable to speak as the tears flowed.

Mirka, who first met her husband during the 2000 Sydney Olympics when she was a talented junior star herself, was chosen by Federer to introduce him to the stage in Newport, and opened her speech by joking that she had been the ‘older woman’ at 21 years old to his 18.

‘When we met, he had exactly zero ATP titles. Zero,’ she said. ‘Looking back, I suppose I was there for all 103 that followed. We shared quite the journey.’

Although Mirka was a constant presence on the tour and witness to the titanic effort her husband put into becoming one of the greatest of all time, she added that ‘tennis was never what impressed me the most.’

Roger Federer was in floods of tears after his wife's speech at his Hall of Fame induction

Federer's wife Mirka introduced him to the stage as he was officially inducted in Newport, RI

‘The man behind it all is even more remarkable,’ she continued. ‘He's the most devoted father that our four children could ever ask for.

‘When I found out we were expecting twins for the first time, I told Roger that my traveling days were probably over. Without missing a beat, he said, “I won't play anymore”. He wasn't being remanded. He meant it. That's who Roger is. His family comes first.

‘Fortunately, we found another solution, and that solution involved babies, strollers, toys, books, and eventually two sets of twins traveling all over the world with us. The tennis tour has always been our home. Our children Myla, Charlene, Leo, and Lenny know him as Papa. The Papa who read bedtime stories, played games with them, who ran their bath, who made them laugh, no matter how busy he was. Whether he won or lost, he always made time for them.

‘I know him always as the kind husband, funny, thoughtful, and endlessly supportive. His parents know him as a loving son. His sister knows him as a wonderful brother. And his friends know him as someone who always has time for them, no matter how busy his life becomes.’

There was barely a dry eye in the house - with Federer’s parents both left in tears - as he stepped onto the stage for his own address.

But Federer was the most overcome as he kissed his wife and accepted the trophy commemorating his induction.

The eight-time Wimbledon champion broke down at a number of different points in his speech, including paying tribute to his mentor, six-time Grand Slam champion Stefan Edberg, and his parents Robert and Lynette.

‘It’s not the first (time),’ he joked as he attempted to pull himself together after calling Edberg his ‘childhood hero’. ‘These are happy tears’.

Join the discussion How has Roger Federer’s legacy shaped what it means to be a true champion on and off the court?

Federer was joined by his kids at the glamorous event in Rhode Island before the US Open

Federer delivered a speech of his own but struggled to fight back tears and deliver his words

The tears flowed as Federer paid tribute to his longest-serving coach Severin Luthi, saying that he ‘kept (him) motivated when (he) needed motivating, and protected (him) when (he) needed protecting.’

‘We’ll get through this,’ he said as the crowd attempting to cheer him on after he broke off. ‘Promise. Until the sun rises!’

As tears streamed down his face while paying tribute to how Martina Navratilova had inspired Mirka to start playing tennis, Federer joked that he needed ‘tissues and sunglasses.’

‘I need everything to protect me,’ before saying: ‘Oh God. Oh my God. I’m going to do the Mirka bit. This is such a mess.’

‘As you know, Mirka is my wife, which is the greatest understatement I can make,’ he began. ‘She's also been my coach, my hitting partner before matches, and my reality check, also my stylist. I definitely needed one at the time.

‘Mirka is the person who showed me how to get more focused about tennis and take joy in everything else. A wonderful mother to our four kids. She and I grab each other's hands and we run through walls. So she's all of these things, and that's my Hall of Fame.’

When able to control his sobbing, the living legend interspersed his learnings from his storied career with witty quips, including the note that the over ‘5,000 headbands’ he had spotted during his career were ‘more than Bjorn Borg and John McEnroe combined’.

But most memorable was his message to players on the tour and future stars, where he encouraged them give back to communities by ‘sharing their passion’, and pushing the game to new heights.

‘We all leave the court eventually, but the sport keeps evolving, and as the pace of professional tennis speeds up, as the sport becomes even more global, I so hope it will keep some of that amateur spirit, keep the camaraderie among the players,’ he said.

‘I hope the players will stay young at heart and stay true to their authentic selves, and always remember: never stop asking questions or taking risks, do things with the game we've never seen before. Keep pushing this sport we love to the next level, and keep getting better, better, and better.’

Sports.title: Everton owners have eroded trust over Harrison Armstrong and Iliman Ndiaye sagas - now they must win back the fans... and manager David Moyes, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Everton owners have eroded trust over Harrison Armstrong and Iliman Ndiaye sagas - now they must win back the fans... and manager David Moyes, writes LEWIS STEELE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

When The Friedkin Group were handed the keys to Everton in December 2024, they could have walked into any pub by Goodison Park or the swanky new waterfront stadium and had a queue of thousands trying to buy them a pint.

Their arrival was a rescue act similar to supremo Dan Friedkin’s mission in the blockbuster Christopher Nolan film Dunkirk, where he was the stunt pilot flying a Spitfire to save Allied soldiers on the beaches. The American billionaires had given Everton a leg-up after years of financial worry.

Now, the Friedkins would probably get an earful of abuse. Frontman Dan need not worry about that, mind – nearly two years after buying the club, he has still not been seen anywhere near a match.

That, in itself, is indicative of an ownership group detached from reality, which was thrust into evidence this weekend amid fan mutiny.

There has been something of a civil war brewing for several weeks at Everton but it escalated intensely on Saturday morning when reports emerged that the club was planning to cash in on 19-year-old homegrown midfielder Harrison Armstrong.

Everton's owners have seriously damaged the trust fans have in them after flirting with the sale of Harrison Armstrong

The next day, the club agreed to sell Iliman Ndiaye, one of their best players alongside Kieran Dewsbury-Hall, Jarrad Branthwaite and Jordan Pickford.

It was not the fine details of the proposed Armstrong exit that mattered but the principle.

Armstrong is not going to suddenly take the club to the Champions League on his own this term, nor is he the second coming of academy graduate Wayne Rooney and, prima facie, the mooted £40million fee might be good business for a player with 24 first-team appearances and zero goals.

But he is the best talent produced in some time from a faltering academy which was set back several years by the previous owners plunging the club into a financial pickle meaning they had to sell their best youngsters and were not able to invest properly in the development teams.

Because of that, versatile and hard-working Armstrong represents a sunflower sprouting in an acre of concrete wasteland. He represents a role model to every other kid in the academy. A Scouse heartbeat of the team living out most fans’ dreams of playing for their boyhood club.

Supporters who made the arduous trip to a rainy Bournemouth rightly voted with their voices before, during and after the 1-1 draw by singing about rioting if the club sold Armstrong. Fan power eventually won with the club pulling the plug on the move.

Daily Mail Sport understands the board was unanimous having considered the offer put on the table from Forest. On Sunday morning, calls were made to the Midlands club to inform them that Armstrong would be staying put.

So that’s that, then, TFG would hope. It does not work like that, Mr Friedkin. Trust is a precious commodity which takes significant time to build up but just seconds to erode.

Two years after buying the club, owner Dan Friedkin still hasn't been anywhere near a match

If the final days of the transfer window go as Everton fans hope, they might forgive the owners for this embarrassing episode. But they will not forget. The owners not attending games does not help and it is fair to question whether their finger can truly be on the pulse of how the club works.

Although he would never publicly admit it, few could blame David Moyes if he were left irked. This appears to be the nadir of a frustrating month for the Scot.

Let’s rewind slightly. Moyes has cut a dejected figure in press conferences this season and body-language experts might describe him as in a sulk. Some fans have picked up on it and were aggrieved at him last week for his comments on the importance of cup competitions.

But the last few days have seen supporters understand why he has looked grumpy. It is clear the manager and the hierarchy are somewhat at odds.

This began when chief executive Angus Kinnear said in an interview with BBC Radio Merseyside that last season was a ‘failure’ when Everton flirted with returning to European football but ultimately missed out.

That would be a fair comment in, say, a couple of years had the board backed Everton in the transfer window. As it stands, though, 14 top-flight clubs have spent more money this summer, according to the online Transfermarkt database.

There are a lot of moving parts in the final days of the window but Ndiaye, one of the club’s best players, now looks likely to leave. They have needed a right back for well over a year but have waited until the final days of this summer to agree a £9.4m deal for Kenny Tete, 30, from Fulham.

Ndiaye is extremely talented and at £60m, Tottenham have got a bargain. Moyes values players who can keep the ball, relieving pressure on team-mates, and he will certainly be losing one of those. Richarlison, 29, will come the other way for £35m.

It is easy to sympathise with David Moyes when you understand his frustrations with bosses

The owners could justifiably claim that Ndiaye has turned down offers of a new contract and that cashing in at some point was a sensible – perhaps inevitable - move. But it would be an easier sell to fans had Ndiaye had pushed to join a team like Real Madrid or Manchester City or Arsenal – and if they had received an eye-watering sum a month ago, with plenty of time to recruit a replacement. But days before the end of the window for such a small fee? Supporters and Moyes are right to question the ambition of TFG.

This summer should have been about strengthening the attack, not letting their best attacker go. Striker Thierno Barry has started the season well, with four goals in three games, but the youngster is not yet consistent and a real No 9 would have transformed last season.

After beating Chelsea on March 21, Everton were three points off the Champions League spots but did not win another game and fell down the table. The feeling was that, with a few more players, they could take that next step and become a disruptor to the so-called Big Six.

But clearly the board had other ideas and maybe their hand has been forced by squad cost ratio.

Some fans that have become aggrieved with Moyes but in declaring after the Bournemouth game ‘the manager is an Evertonian’ he demonstrated he wants fans to know he understands how they feel.

Had the boss had his way this summer, he might have already signed striker Folarin Balogun from Monaco, or defenders Ola Aina from Nottingham Forest or Guela Doue at Strasbourg.

Perhaps alarm bells should have sounded earlier this month when a £2m deal for Manchester United’s Ethan Wheatley – eyed as a prospect who could make an impact in the first team - fell down with Everton citing finances.

Yet the window has not been a catastrophe. The signing of Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough is shrewd business, while Moyes likes Brennan Johnson who can play across the front three. Tyrique George, who made a loan from Chelsea permanent, has impressed this summer.

Letting Iliman Ndiaye leave for Tottenham for £60million at this stage of the summer is poor

Richarlison and last year’s loanee Jack Grealish look poised to return to the club. Both would be marquee signings — if Ndiaye was not being let go on the cheap — and are fan favourites but they are now aged 29 and 30 with sketchy injury records.

Tete, too, is an experienced asset who Moyes tried to buy last year. All three are good players but potentially past their peak years and recruitment of younger players would likely have left the club in a stronger position to reach their goals in the long-term.

Fans hoped for a window where Everton made the next step in their pursuit of European football and maybe winning a first trophy since 1995. Newcastle, Crystal Palace, West Ham and Aston Villa have all shown how to do it in the last few years.

Instead, with comments from the CEO about ‘failure’ and an ownership seemingly out of touch with the fanbase, Moyes will be left with more questions than answers when the window slams shut.

One answer we do have, though, is the reason for why the Everton manager has worn an upside down smile in public so far this season. Just like that, the Toffees are back to having a hierarchy on trial with the fans.

Sports.title: Where next for Moses Itauma? Filip Hrgovic's savage verdict has shattered the Mike Tyson hype as Britain's fallen prodigy begins his long road back, writes JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
The most alarming contribution to the inquest into the slaying of Moses came from the national hero of Croatia who was the real story of a Saturday night at the O2 which was dark for British boxing but dazzling to behold.

Filip Hrgovic said of our young Itauma: ‘No, I didn’t feel his power.’

That will be as devastating to the lad previously hailed as the next Mike Tyson as James Bond being told he is no longer attractive to women.

It will hurt even more than the punches which sent him reeling from domination to defeat and hospital on the evening he was supposed to become the second youngest world heavyweight champion of all time.

Power has been Moses Itauma’s middle name since he began felling giants like saplings. Suddenly, at 21, he is being likened to Samson who lost his mythological strength when he had a haircut.

Were there clues in how Hrgovic survived the first eight rounds of this IBF world title fight and countless punches, every one of which looked as if it would have knocked out a horse?

Moses Itauma saw his hope of becoming the second youngest heavyweight world champion ended by Filip Hrgovic

Hrgovic, right, declared afterwards that he 'didn't feel his power' in another blow to Itauma

To suggest as much would be to downplay the superhuman heart and phenomenal resilience of chin with which Hrgovic realised his own lifelong ambition of global glory. Just in time at 34.

Nevertheless, Itauma could not finish him off. Which brings other factors into issue. It is concerning, also, that Britain’s young lion should gas out on the first time in his career he was required to go beyond six rounds. Trainer Ben Davison finds himself under inquisition as to whether presumption of another early KO left Moses short on stamina build-up. Or did he simply punch himself out?

Whatever the reason, it was worrying to see one so young that exhausted as he staggered to extinction as early as the ninth round. Certainly Hrgovic put into words what many of us felt. That he was beaten in a large part by experience. The new champion who had vowed to ‘smash the kid’s face and send him back to high school’ had this to say after he had done just that: ‘He is a tremendous talent but he boxed like an amateur and must learn to fight like a professional.

‘With more experience he would have known he was winning every round and what he should have done was box out the fight to a points decision behind his jab. Not keep trying to knock me out. Although I did know he would tire the longer the fight went.’

But no power in his punches? Of being dropped once, a flash knock-down in the second round, Hrgovic said: ‘I didn’t feel it. He is very fast and caught me off balance with a punch I didn’t see.’

And so it would come to pass that in the battle of their ages it was from the kid’s corner that the white towel came fluttering in. By then not to great surprise. As early as the fifth round Itauma was beginning to grimace at the physical demands being made of him and the heavy hits he, too, was taking. In the eighth he launched a desperate assault which Hrgovic not only rode out but also inflicted damage of his own.

To his credit Itauma prodded out some punches at the start of the ninth but looked more like a fish floundering out of water. Hrgovic speared him with what he called ‘strength which came from Jesus Christ’.

So what next for he who was hailed as the next Mike Tyson? Hrgovic’s advice: ‘Several easier fights to gain more experience and rebuild his confidence. And I do think that with his speed of hand he will become a world champion one day.’

Hrgovic highlighted how he had used his experience to see off the challenge of Itauma

Hrgovic showed phenomenal resilience to achieve his lifelong dream at the age of 34

Hrgovic advised Itauma to take some easier fights to rebuild his confidence after the defeat

Promoter Frank Warren sympathised: ‘A first defeat does take away that aura of invincibility and we will give Moses the time it takes to recover from that. He is still a very special talent.’

Meanwhile, heavyweight life goes on. Warren has announced October 17 at the O2 for a lip-smacking WBO world-title rematch of the thunderous Battle of Britain between champion Daniel Dubois and white-collar graduate Fabio Wardley. Hrgovic will make his first championship defence against Cuba’s mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez and makes a prediction when he says: ‘I want to go on to a title unification fight against Daniel.’

And may it please the lords of the ring that Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury get their act together in November, whether it be in London or New York.

It will be some while before Itauma rejoins the fray, from the back of the queue. He went home from hospital the morning after his downfall to begin recuperation from the battering and also a leg injured as he reeled against the ropes.

The psychological wounds will take much longer to heal. Though it is not impossible. Muhammad Ali, Joe Louis, Joe Frazier, George Foreman and Lennox Lewis – to name but a few – all lost more than one fight and came back as champions.

But Moses Itauma the next Mike Tyson? Even as Filip Hrgovic goes home to a much-deserved hero’s welcome in Zagreb, one thing we do know for sure is that if the original Iron Mike had landed just one of the punches he took on Saturday night, he would have been knocked out.

Sports.title: NFL fraudster Daejon Love deemed a 'serious flight risk' as prosecutors urge judge to keep him behind bars after $1.3m swindle was uncovered
Sports.content:
Prosecutors are pushing to keep alleged fraudster Daejon Love behind bars after his $1.3million romance scam was revealed.

Love is accused of falsely claiming to be a member of the San Francisco 49ers in an attempt to swindle multiple women he met on dating apps to prop up fake investments.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, prosecutors are asking a judge to keep Love detained - arguing that evidence against him is strong and he has 'every incentive to flee.'

On Friday, it was announced by the Department of Justice that Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and alleged accomplice, Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, were arrested earlier this week at an airport in Boise, Idaho.

The criminal complaint, obtained by the Daily Mail, lays out evidence against Love - including an alleged lie to at least one woman that he was related to Jordan Love, the quarterback for the Green Bay Packers.

Additionally, Daejon falsely claimed he had relationships with Tyreek Hill, Antonio Brown and John Brown.

Prosecutors are requesting that alleged fraudster Daejon Love remain behind bars as he poses a "flight risk" as his fraud case unfolds

Love (pictured) and alleged accomplice Taylor Jamie Chan were arrested earlier this week at an airport in Boise, Idaho and charged with defrauding dozens of women out of millions

In the complaint, details of Love's scheme with one woman revealed that he convinced her to send him $17,200 after they met on Tinder in March of 2025. The two went on a date, with Love later asking 'about her financial situation and if she was interested in investing.'

'[The woman] did not receive any confirmation of the investments,' the complaint said. 'When [the woman] asked Love about the investments, Love stopped communicating with her.'

Per the court filing, Love claimed to have exercised with various NFL players - including Hill and Brown. The filing also says Love claimed to have received 'invitations to try out with NFL teams' before he 'chose' the 49ers.

The federal complaint - which was filed in Portland, Oregon - reveals Love and Chan have been charged with wire fraud and conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

The criminal complaint shows that, beginning in February 2022, Love and Chan allegedly created fake investment opportunities to defraud women in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California.

It's alleged that Love initiated contact with most of the women through online dating apps while Chan would pose as Love's financial adviser to gain their victims' trust and talk victims through prospective investments.

Love allegedly also created fake bank and investment accounts and balances, which he would flaunt to victims in an effort to legitimize the alleged scheme.

The pair allegedly also exchanged investment-related messages, in which Chan played the role of Love's investment advisor. Love allegedly would screenshot Chan's messages and send them to victims to convince them to part with their money.

He allegedly pretended to be a relative of Packers quarterback Jordan Love as part of the ruse

Ex-Dolphins star Tyreek Hill was among the NFL players Love claimed he was friends with

Love is pictured wearing 49ers-branded headwear din a photo from his now-deleted Instagram

The pair also hosted three-way FaceTime calls in which they displayed falsified gains to victims, according to the criminal complaint.

As well as sending money they thought was being invested, victims also loaned Love large amounts.

If they didn't have money to invest, Love allegedly instructed victims to take out personal loans with the promise they would quickly get repaid.

Once they had no more money to invest, or if they asked too many questions, Love allegedly blocked his victims but kept their money.

He has used several names including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love, and Jordan Love to perpetuate the scheme, according to the criminal complaint.

Of the victims that have so far been identified and interviewed, none have received any returns.

Financial records show Love and Chan received around $1.3m from their victims, according to the criminal complaint. There have been 26 identified. The FBI, however, believes there are far more.

Love would falsely portray himself as a wealthy individual, often as a 49ers player or a real estate investor, before flaunting his lavish lifestyle to unsuspecting victims

They also created fake bank and investment accounts and balances, which they would flaunt to victims in an effort to legitimize the scheme

After the scheme was revealed, the internet mocked Love - with 49ers passing game coach Leonard Hankerson posting this AI altered image of himself and the alleged fraudster

The FBI discovered that, on August 24, Chan was flying from California to meet up with Love in Boise. Love was in Idaho allegedly to meet new victims and officers swooped to apprehend both of them at an airport.

In the days since the scheme was uncovered, social media has mocked Love and his 'ties' to the 49ers.

Even Niners passing game coach Leonard Hankerson joined in with jokes, using AI to create a fake image of Love standing next to him on the field.

Former San Francisco pass catcher Kendrick Bourne went to the comments and joked, 'Man I knew you was coaching him [laughing emojis].'

Hankerson replied, 'Man I hate we lost him.... He was balling!!!'

Others have created similar fake images of themselves signing NFL contracts or practicing to join in on the internet dogpile.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk speaks out on Liverpool's transfer strategy that could force out Cody Gakpo
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk speaks out on Liverpool's transfer strategy that could force out Cody Gakpo

Liverpool have continued their pursuit of forward signings and as they close in on Bradley Barcola Cody Gakpo could leave Anfield with Manchester City circling

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo could leave before the window closes

Virgil van Dijk insists Liverpool should look to keep Cody Gakpo because the club "should keep quality players" as a move to Manchester City gathers momentum.

‌



The Dutchman could ultimately prove to be the one who loses out in the Reds' summer recruitment drive as they finally close in on Bradley Barcola from PSG. The Frenchman has been on their radar for months and a £123million agreement has finally been struck.

‌



Barcola though would play in Gakpo's position on the wing and as a result Liverpool are prepared to green light his departure. Tottenham had been keen but the Dutchman is more likely to move to City in a deal that could reach £85m.

‌



Gakpo was on target in Liverpool's opening weekend draw at Newcastle and outshone both Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - two men who cost in excess of £100m - and Van Dijk is clearly adamant he should remain at Anfield.

When quizzed on whether his compatriot should stay he replied: "What do you think? He's a quality player. I think we should keep quality players. Let's see what the next few days bring. I want him to stay not only because he's a quality player but also because he's a friend of mine. He's very important for us."

‌



Gakpo's departure will only sanctioned if Liverpool sign another wide forward, in addition to Barcola, reports ESPN. But the Reds have been active in that space and are currently eyeing Ismaila Sarr.

They moved onto the Crystal Palace winger after it became clear that Brighton had no plans to sell Yankuba Minteh, who they had originally gone after before seeing their bids rejected.

View 2 Images Liverpool look set to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: PSG via Getty Images)

‌



Gakpo moved to Liverpool after the World Cup in 2022 and has gone on to score 51 times in 182 games without ever establishing himself as the team's marquee marksman. The signing of Isak for a British record fee has meant that Liverpool have had to seek a return on their investment.

The same can be said for Wirtz and, if he arrives, Barcola. Iraola would have a front three who were all signed for fees than exceeded the £100m mark whilst they also have Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, adding further competition in the final third.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez lays down the gauntlet to Chelsea's Premier League title rivals
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez lays down the gauntlet to Chelsea's Premier League title rivals

Emiliano Martinez was straight into the Chelsea XI just a day after completing his £7.5m move from Aston Villa - and is adamant his side have genuine title aspirations

View 2 Images New Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez after the win over Brighton

Emiliano Martinez insisted he has joined Chelsea to win the title after getting off to a winning start.

‌



Chelsea made it two straight wins in the Premier League after their seven-goal thriller with Brighton at Stamford Bridge.

‌



World Cup winner Martinez was rushed straight into the team after completing his £7.5m switch from Aston Villa and the Argentina No1 has already set high targets.

‌



Martinez shipped three goals but says the forward line of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro can help them mount a serious title challenge.

Chelsea keeper Martinez said: “I am here for a reason. "I spoke with Chelsea legends John Terry and Petr Cech. I know how big this club is and what we want to achieve this season. I came here to help.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“I had an amazing seven years at Aston Villa. I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League.

“The front three is amazing. When we go forward, we can hurt teams. We had a lot of chances to finish the game. Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro had chances to kill the game. At the back, we need to bring the goals down.

“I trained only one day with the team. The guys have treated me really well in the last day or two. I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity in the back.

‌



“A win is a win. I know it wasn't a perfect game. But in the end, winning and moving on is what we need. We've got 36 games left and it's one week after another.”

View 2 Images Chelsea made it two wins from two after beating Brighton 4-3

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso added: “I want to win, whatever it takes to win and each game can be different so we need to prepare for the best, we need to train for the best and be prepared for whatever scenario we have.

‌



“So it's not that this is going to be replicated against Arsenal next week. Today it was a big challenge and it was a big test and next Sunday it's going to be a big one but we can continue progressing on the good things and correcting the other ones that we can do better.”

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said: “Overall we really had the opportunity to take something from here with this performance. We dominated the game, had the ball, created plenty of chances.”

Sports.title: Arsenal primed for chaotic end to window with winger signing and three exits agreed
Sports.content:
Arsenal primed for chaotic end to window with winger signing and three exits agreed

Arsenal are having to sanction several exits in the final days of the transfer window with some of their fringe players, Gabriel Martinelli among them, seeking pastures new

View 3 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are both poised to leave Arsenal (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

Arsenal haven't rested on their laurels this summer and despite completing some blockbuster deals the club have still been active ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

‌



The Premier League champions looked in total control in their opening game as they hammered Coventry City at the Emirates. They did so with new signing Christos Tzolis impressing from the left wing following his summer move from Club Brugge.

‌



Mikel Arteta was without Bruno Guimaraes, who was dealing with an injury which meant he couldn't take up his role in midfield, whilst Ezri Konsa wasn't signed and registered in time from Aston Villa. He could make his debut on Monday night against his former club.

‌



Arsenal's arrivals has left them with a star-studded squad, but one that ultimately has too many senior players for even a matchday squad. Arteta has bemoaned the fact he's had to leave certain players out, suggesting the authorities should increase the size of the benches.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He had claimed that certain absentees, the likes of Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli, were still part of his plans, but with days left in the window both are poised to depart.

‌



Brazilian duo among three to exit

Jesus looks to have landed himself a sensational move to Barcelona having been linked with a switch to Italy for much of the summer. The Spanish champions will pay £8.4million for the 29-year-old, who had entered the final year of his contract.

Jesus was one of the signings that saw Arsenal turn into title contenders when he joined from Manchester City in 2022. He was initially a regular but over the years has seen his role decrease, in part owing to injury, and now has Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz ahead of him in the pecking order.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has been forced to let some of his attacking player leave such is the depth of his squad (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



Compatriot Gabriel Martinelli was alongside Jesus in a front three that also included Bukayo Saka when Arsenal first challenged for the Premier League under Arteta. But, like Jesus, his role has been impacted by the club's constant desire to add more firepower.

Unlike Jesus, who Arsenal will make a loss on, Martinelli stands to represent a huge profit having been signed as an unknown quantity. A £60m switch to Saudi Arabia is now close.

Another fringe player in Fabio Vieira, who was signed in 2022 but has made just five league starts in that time, is set for a permanent switch to Hamburg. He had spent last season on loan at the Bundesliga side and is now set to call them home moving forward.

‌



Winger signed as Alvarez saga drags on

Even with Jesus and Martinelli set to leave, Arteta can still look to the likes of Gyokeres, Havertz, Saka, Tzolis, Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Martin Odegaard and Ethan Nwaneri as options in the final third.

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez has been pushing for the exit door at Atletico Madrid (Image: (Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Despite that they've still agreed a £4m deal for young Georgian winger Andria Bartishvili. The teenager was also on Liverpool's radar but has opted for a switch to the capital.

‌



Julian Alvarez's saga has dragged on all summer and, despite skipping Atletico Madrid training this week, the club are adamant he will not be sold to Barcelona. The Catalan's pursuit of Jesus does fill the void they had in their attack, which they had hoped Alvarez would fill.

If the Argentine does want to leave Atletico it would appear as though Arsenal are his only option. Diego Simeone is still prepared to welcome him back and Alvarez has returned to training, which would indicate he's much closer to staying rather than heading back to the Premier League.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit

Arsenal have spent a considerable amount this summer as they attempt to defend their Premier League crown but a few title winners could potentially be on the way out of the Emirates over the coming days

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli is set to earn Arsenal a record amount (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli is set to leave the Emirates and join Al-Hilal for a record £55m. The Brazilian winger has been linked with a move away from North London throughout the summer.

‌



Saudi side Al-Hilal had emerged as suitors over recent days and had been holding talks with the Gunners in an effort to secure a deal. And it appears that they have done just that.

‌



According to reports, Martinelli is set to fly over to the Middle East over the next few days to undergo a medical and complete a move worth around €65m (£55.7m) ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

‌



Should the move go through as expected, it would see Arsenal bank their highest fee ever for a sale, smashing the £35m that they received from Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain back in 2017.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Asked about Martinelli's future in his pre-match press conference, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: "That's another personal situation that we're dealing with. I think everybody knows and recognises how much we love Gabi. Whatever the outcome is, it will be because everybody agrees to that."

‌



Martinelli joined Arsenal from Brazilian side Ituano in 2019 and he has gone on to score 62 goals in 278 appearances in all competitions. He helped the club win the Premier League last season.

Martinelli is not the only league winner set to leave the club over the coming days. Striker Gabriel Jesus is anticipated to complete a switch to Barcelona.

Asked why the forward was not in training, Arteta said: "It's something to do with the numbers that we have in the squad at the moment and the way we're managing that kind of situation individually with all the players - they have some personal situations."

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus is also expected to quit Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if he had held conversations with either Martinelli or Jesus, Arteta replied: "Yes, for sure. Those conversations go both ways, but I'm very satisfied with how these conversations went because I know what is in each other's hearts, and the words that come through in those conversations make me really happy.

"But it's inevitable at some point you need to have certain discussions and say certain things that sometimes are tough."

‌



Along with Jesus and Martinelli, Fabio Vieira is also set to depart, with talks over an £8.6m move to Hamburg advancing.

Leandro Trossard, Christian Norgaard and Jakub Kiwior have all left North London over recent weeks, while academy graduate Reiss Nelson saw his deal cancelled by mutual consent. Arsenal have refreshed their side with a number of big-money signings including Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie.

Sports.title: Arsenal strike Gabriel Jesus transfer agreement with Barcelona as fee revealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal strike Gabriel Jesus transfer agreement with Barcelona as fee revealed

Arsenal forward Gabriel Jesus is set to join Barcelona before the end of the transfer window after the Gunners agreed a deal with the La Liga giants

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus is set to depart Arsenal (Image: Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Arsenal have agreed on an £8.57million transfer for Gabriel Jesus to join Barcelona. The Gunners stand to earn further remuneration in add-ons as the forward makes the switch to La Liga.

‌



Jesus has trained away from Mikel Arteta's first team and not been included in either of the north London side's matchday squads this term, after being made available for transfer. The Brazilian has been linked to an exit throughout the summer, with Napoli among the suitors, but Arsenal's asking price had previously proven problematic.

‌



Jesus arrived at the Emirates from Manchester City in 2022 and was viewed as a transformative signing. As Arsenal have progressed, the 29-year-old has struggled for minutes due to increased competition and injuries.

‌



His spell at Arsenal has seen him score 32 goals and provide 22 assists across 123 appearances but now he is set to move. Arteta has previously hinted that Jesus was destined to say farewell, referring to 'personal situations' after leaving him out of the team.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Well, it's something to do with the numbers that we have in the squad at the moment and the way we're managing that kind of situation individually with all the players that have some personal situations," Arteta said in a press conference.

‌



Asked to clarify what he meant by 'personal situations', Arteta added: "Personal situations, whatever they are, I think it's clear."

Jesus is unlikely to be alone in saying goodbye to his Arsenal team-mates in the coming days. Countryman Gabriel Martinelli looks set to join Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal before the end of the window.

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus has just a year left on his Arsenal contract (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The Gunners are said to have agreed a deal worth up to £55.7m for the sale of the winger. The fees will serve as a significant boost for any final business Arsenal wish to undertake.

Arteta's side have been in touch over the possibility of a move for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez and are open to completing a transfer. However, they will only do so if they believe the forward is committed to such a deal.

Alvarez has been keen to move to Barcelona to complete his 'dream', but Atletico have refused to deal with their La Liga rivals.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"The members of Atletico Madrid’s Board of Directors have unanimously expressed their full support for the club’s decision not to negotiate the transfer of Julian Alvarez to FC Barcelona," Atletico said in a statement.

"The members of the Board of Directors are aware that: Atletico Madrid is open to negotiations that are part of the transfer market, but always in an ethical and professional manner and with respect between clubs.

‌



"We fully support the position previously communicated by the club that FC Barcelona have not met these requirements and, as a result, there have been no negotiations, nor will there be any negotiations with them regarding the transfer of Julián Alvarez.”

Alvarez returned to training after missing Atletico's most recent match and must decide whether he prefers to remain at the club following a frosty reception from supporters.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
